| 122 | **Wallet re-architected into one command-centre page — a luminous balance hero, a sliding dashboard sheet, every money action in a dialog (2026-09-29). SUPERSEDES the presentation of Decisions #55 / #60 / #63 (wallet); the finance backend, `/api/wallet/*` and `@projective/types/finance` are kept.** **(A) One page.** The wallet's lane, header band, footer rig and seven deep pages are purged with every presentation file (19 components, 19 islands, 11 stylesheets, 14 core modules, 7 routes). `/wallet` is a bare canvas — `(dashboard)/_layout.tsx` resolves no lane or band for it — holding ONE island, `WalletHome`: a hero pinned `position: sticky` under the top bar and a rounded dashboard sheet that overlaps the hero's lower edge by a negative margin and slides over it in the native window scroll. The hero pins only on viewports at least 36rem tall, because on a shorter one a pinned hero makes its own lower half unreachable, and a control focused under the sheet scrolls the hero back into view. The retired deep pages answer a thin `[section].tsx` with a **308** to a section of the one page, keeping `w` and `display` (`transactions` → `#transactions`, `activity` → `#cash-flow`, `payouts` · `funding` · `invoices` · `access` → `#upcoming`, `methods` → `#methods`); any other segment is a 404. **(B) The hero:** a scope pill (the account and the currency it is HELD in; a popover of real `?w=` links); the total through `MoneyView` at a fluid size floored at `--text-3xl`, its weight overridden to `--fw-medium`; Available · In escrow · Clearing (+ On hold only when non-zero), each explained by a Tooltip and a visually-hidden sentence; four glass pills (Top up · Transfer · Withdraw · Split) with the rest in a More menu. A capability-absent action is ABSENT; a verification- or processor-blocked one is rendered-and-LOCKED and opens an explainer naming the reason (the #60 rule); a single overflow action becomes its own pill rather than a one-item menu. **(C) The sheet:** Accounts rail (personal · tax pot · vaults · the "All accounts" rollup, each tile a real `?w=` link); Cash flow (Week · Month · Quarter · Year mirrored into `?flow=`, the totals as the legend, CSS bars of money in over money out on ONE shared peak with a keyboard ⁄ pointer readout and a visually-hidden table twin, colours run through the dataviz validator); Upcoming (verification · spend approvals with Approve ⁄ Decline · bills · fundable stages · escrow holds · clearing releases with a progress ring · recurring rules · the payout schedule · the smoother, each carrying only the actions the server offered); Transactions (Today · Yesterday · Earlier from the server's own date label; a row opens its detail; Load more; CSV export); Payment methods. Every write is a `Dialog` — a bottom sheet at ≤767px — running compose → review → commit with an idempotency key per attempt, one dialog at a time (a new one replaces, never stacks). **(D) Backend, additive and presentation-only:** `ActivityRange` gains `7d` (Week); the overview's escrow holds are GROUPED PER STAGE and labelled `project · stage` — a stage holds one escrow per funded ticket, so two tickets rendered as two identical rows while the hero said "Held on 1 active stage"; the business `invoicesDueAmount` is summed in the held currency and converted once — per-invoice conversion printed £48,818.89 beside an escrow total of £48,818.90, the rounding class the file's own comment forbids. Registry glyphs `arrow-up-right`, `arrow-down-left` and `repeat` (§B.7.1). **(E) A package defect found by measurement:** under `dir="rtl"` every `MoneyView` scrambled — "£3,414.25" rendered "25.3,414£" and "−£7,086.61" rendered "61.7,086£ −" — because a split figure's sign · symbol · major · minor are flex children that reverse, after which the bidi algorithm reorders the digits. `.ui-money__amount` and `.ui-money__origin` are now isolated left-to-right (the `PaymentCard` card-number technique), recorded as a §A.6 "Figures" row; this corrects every money figure on every surface under RTL. **Defects in this pass's own work, found by measurement and fixed:** the hero printed "£27,036.30" beside a "Personal · USD" pill with nothing reconciling the two (the total is a DERIVED figure and carries no origin) — a "Converted from USD" disclosure with the rate in its Tooltip; the pill's currency measured 4.21:1 and the dark hero's labels 4.46–4.48:1 at 390px (the dark brand teal lifts the glow) — full ink for the currency, a softer dark glow and a firmer soft ink, now ≥4.63:1 in all four states; the phone pill row laid out unevenly because a Tooltip wraps a locked pill in an inline anchor, so only the bare More button took `flex: 1` — an equal-column grid; the payout-schedule dialog always opened on "Monthly" and sent `instant: false`, so Save would have silently rewritten a Threshold schedule — it now opens on the current one; the ledger detail disclosed the original amount twice; zero cash-flow totals read "+£0.00"; Net printed a hyphen beside Money out's true minus; a refused Continue showed one error at a time — every invalid field now marks at once and focus moves to the first. **Verified in a real browser against the live local stack**, four seeded views (a personal seller, a team-vault owner, a business-vault owner, the read-only rollup) at 1440 and 390, light and dark, LTR and RTL: zero horizontal overflow in either direction, zero console errors, hero text ≥4.63:1, pills 44px tall on desktop and an even 84×74 grid on a phone, the phone dialog a full-width sheet docked at the viewport bottom; the locked explainer, More menu, ledger detail, payout schedule and the Split preview (40/30/30 stakes); `?flow=` switching (7 and 12 bars off `range=7d` ⁄ `12m`) and the keyboard readout; the section redirects; and ONE real write — a US$1.00 transfer (Kwame's personal wallet → North Loop) that posted with its idempotency key and refreshed the hero (£4,119.87 → £4,119.08) and a new Today band in place (the local seed keeps it; `deno task db:reset` restores). `deno task check` exit 0, `deno lint` clean over 1,741 files, unit **1,645 passed ⁄ 4 failed** — the four pre-existing `theme-engine.test.ts` failures (#96(a)); the 11 new wallet tests pass. **No DB migration**, no lifecycle change, and no Dev Context axis (the old wallet axes were already removed by the "Remove mocks" commits; layout direction stays global). **FLAGGED — surface, do not silently resolve:** (a) **the brief's hexes (`#288690`, `#3B1262`) were not used** — §3 is token-only, so the gradient runs `--primary` into a `--tertiary`-derived indigo; the brief's own formula `color-mix(in srgb, var(--primary) 70%, #3B1262)` evaluates to a petrol blue rather than a purple, and the theme has no purple ramp. (b) **Two recorded, scoped exceptions need the owner's ratification:** the design language forbids a "purple-blue hero blur", and §B.4.3 allows glass only on pinned bars, floating sheets and marks over photography — the hero and its glass pills are neither, and ship at the brief's direction, scoped to `.wlt-hero` (noted in DESIGN_SYSTEM). (c) **"Exchange" has no backend capability** — the fourth pill is Split where the server offers it, else More. (d) The brief's role and date "badges" are inline meta text and a progress ring — §B.11 forbids a pill for non-actionable metadata. (e) **Capabilities no longer surfaced on the wallet:** the Standing gauge, the business burn-down and spending caps, the access matrix and audit log, statement and invoice history, payout history, and the team split roster (its stakes survive in the Split dialog). Their endpoints remain; bringing any back is a product decision. (f) Escrow rows are converted per stage while the hero converts the sum, so a row can differ from the metric by a penny — inherent to converting at two granularities. (g) `live-wallet.ts` still mints `/wallet/transactions` and `/wallet/payouts` hrefs — harmless through the 308s, but they should name the sections. | 123 | **Wallet polish — the hero behind the glass chrome, a header band with the range ruler, the four-state allocation meter, the Finance drawer, and the MoneyView minor-digit baseline (2026-09-29). REFINES Decision #122.** **(A) The hero runs behind the chrome.** `.wlt-hero` pulls itself up by `--wlt-hero-lift` (top bar + header band) and pads its content back down by the same amount, so the glass top bar and band show the aurora while every control starts below them and stays clickable; it stays an in-flow box in the window scroll, sticky at `top: 0` only where the viewport is ≥ 36rem tall. The lift is declared ON the hero, not `:root` — a custom property that reads another resolves where it is declared, so a `:root` lift never saw the band height the frame sets. The two shell frames between the hero and the chrome clip their overflow; they are released on the BLOCK axis only while they hold the wallet (`.ui-shell-frame:has(.wlt-hero)`), keeping the inline clip that contains wide rigs. **(B) A header band returns, from the URL alone.** `walletHeaderFor` (composed into `middleNavHeaderFor`; no lane, no footer) mounts `WalletBand`: a segmented **range ruler** (`7D · 1M · 3M · 6M · 1Y · 5Y · All`, a radiogroup with a sliding thumb positioned from the index alone — no measurement — and mirrored by one sign; the checked cell's own ink carries the state, so a frozen animation clock can never make it lie), a **display-currency trigger** writing the SAME store as the account menu's picker (`commitDisplayCurrency`), an icon link to `/settings`, and the **Finance drawer** toggle. Band and page are two hydration roots joined by client-only signals in `wallet-state.ts` (`walletPeriod` · `walletDrawerOpen` · `walletDisplay`), each root painting its own server-resolved prop until the client says otherwise (the #69 request-race rule). The Cash-flow section lost its own period picker (one control, not two) and names its window in the heading. `ActivityRange` gains `180d` · `5y` · `all` in the Zod SSOT; `activityOf` sizes each window from one table, `all` from the oldest movement read, and `flowSeries` labels a window longer than a year by month AND year. `?flow=` now carries `7d|1m|3m|6m|1y|5y|all`; the pre-ruler names still resolve. **(C) The allocation meter** heads the sheet: one track divided between Available (`--primary`) · Clearing (`--warning`) · In escrow (`--success`) · Reserved (the aurora violet), widths `flex-grow` from the SAME four figures the server summed into the total — set directly, never transitioned — with a 2px surface seam, a glyph + label + share legend (largest-remainder whole percents, `<1%` for a sliver), and a Tooltip per segment carrying figure · share · meaning; hovering one quiets the rest on `opacity` only. One pure `allocationOf` + `fundStateHint` in `wallet-home.ts` feeds the meter AND the hero's metrics, so their order and sentences cannot drift. **(D) The Finance drawer** (package `Drawer`, docked inline-end): the KYC/KYB gate as an `Alert` when one is open; every action the server offers as an icon-first grid (Top up · Transfer · Withdraw · Recurring deposit · Add payment method · Payout schedule, then anything else offered), locked ones rendered-and-explained exactly as in the hero; and records as rows — All transactions and Cash flow scroll to their section and move focus to its heading, and on a business vault **Invoices & statements** opens a new dialog reading `/api/wallet/invoices` (bills due · the accruing month · past statements). No route was added. **(E) Glass and cards.** The scope switcher, the More menu and the currency list are one `wlt-glass-pop` treatment (a `--glass-veil-panel` veil on a `::before` underlay, a hairline, `--radius-xl`, rows hovering as `--radius-md` pills, secondary ink `--on-surface-variant`); the sheet's first `--wlt-sheet-fade` is a blurred veil fading to opaque `--surface`; account tiles take the card contract (`--card-pad` · `--card-radius` · `--surface-1`, no resting border, a `--card-hover-lift` + `--elevation-medium` lift on a link tile only, the rail padded so the lift is not clipped). **(F) MoneyView (package, every surface):** the minor run sits on the major run's BASELINE — no longer raised — sized `var(--minor-size)` and faded `var(--minor-fade)` through per-step `--money-minor-size`/`--money-minor-fade` hooks (hero 0.42em; body and micro unsplit at full ink). Measured: identical baselines at hero/key/body, faded pence ≥ 4.83:1 on the light surface. This reverses the component's documented "never dim the tail" rationale at the owner's direction. **DEFECTS FOUND BY MEASUREMENT, NOT INSPECTION:** (1) the band inherited a column layout because `.wlt-band` already named the ledger's date bands — renamed `.wlt-header`; (2) a drawer action opened its dialog after a fixed 280ms, but the drawer's exit starts a render after the press, so the dialog captured a vanishing drawer button as its return target and focus fell to `<body>` on close — the hand-off now waits for the drawer to leave the DOM and parks focus on the band's toggle first (verified for a pointer-opened drawer too); (3) the sheet's rim and body met at two hard stops on the same offset, leaving an anti-aliased, half-transparent row that read as a dark hairline — the body now starts a step inside the rim; (4) the dataviz validator put the brief's order — brand teal beside success green — at ΔE 14.8, under the 15 a full-colour reader needs, so the states are ordered by how soon the money can be spent (the direction money travels, read backwards), which measures ΔE 19.5, and the hero's metrics follow; (5) the wallet now renders a middle-nav frame, which switched on the top bar's outer frame "L" — and on a phone that L and both fixed frame fills sat at the hidden rail's 64px, the pre-existing Decision #108(e) defect on every framed route: fixed at the root by zeroing `--shell-sidebar-cur-w` on `.ui-app-shell` below `--bp-md` and hiding the outer L there, as the nested seams already were; (6) the owner's `corner-shape: scoop` fillet is one engine's feature — elsewhere it painted a solid block over the content's corner, and it ate pointer events there — redrawn as a radial gradient, logical and mirrored, `pointer-events: none`; (7) the package `Drawer` docked logically but slid physically, so under `dir="rtl"` a closed right drawer rested on-screen — the RTL transforms are mirrored; (8) the gradient commit left `--wlt-hero-glow-*` and `--wlt-hero-midnight` dangling — the glow layers painted nothing (removed) and the lock badge had no ground (re-pointed to `--wlt-hero-deep`); (9) the accruing statement printed "accruing" twice and a past statement's trailing figure was unlabelled. **Verified in-browser** against the live local stack as three seeded personas (a personal seller, a team-vault owner, a business owner) at 1440 · 800 · 390, light + dark, LTR + RTL: zero horizontal overflow everywhere; the ruler by click, arrows and End with the URL and heading following and the thumb landing exactly on the checked cell; a real currency switch through the band (restored to GBP afterwards); four segments at exact proportions (545 · 242 · 363 · 61 of 1,210px); the drawer → dialog → return-focus path; the invoices dialog on live bills; drawer text ≥ 7.77:1 in dark; the detector clean. `deno task check` 0 errors, `deno lint` clean over 1,745 files, unit **1,648 passed ⁄ 4 failed** — the four pre-existing `theme-engine.test.ts` failures (#96(a)); 3 new wallet tests. **No DB migration**, no lifecycle change, no Dev Context axis (the range and the drawer are view state, not a simulatable persona or gate). **FLAGGED — surface, do not silently resolve:** (a) **the brief's hexes (`#288690` · `#268C66` · `#F19C13` · `#A013F1`) were not used** — the meter reads `--primary`/`--success`/`--warning` and the owner's own `--wlt-aurora-violet`; the validator still flags the brand teal's chroma (0.088 < 0.10) and, in dark, the theme's own success/warning as lighter than a categorical band — both pass contrast and both are theme decisions. (b) **"Reserved" is the dispute lockbox only.** The tax pot is a separate sub-wallet and the smoother holds no balance, so neither is in the total; folding them in would make the meter disagree with the figure above it. "On hold" is renamed "Reserved" wallet-wide. (c) **Three exceptions need the owner's ratification** — the translucent sheet rim against the solid-region gate (§3 gate 6), its blur and the glass popovers against functional transparency (gate 9), and the faded pence against MoneyView's prior rationale — each scoped and recorded in `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`. (d) **No KYC/KYB flow exists**, so the gate banner offers a trigger only where the server names a destination or the next step is a wallet action; an unverified account with neither gets the requirement and no button (gate 11). (e) The band's settings icon links `/settings`, still a placeholder page. (f) The brief's "Financial & Burn-Down Analytics" row is labelled **Cash flow** and lands there: the burn-down is not surfaced (#122(e)). Invoices & statements is business-only because the backend returns nothing for any other wallet, and no statement has a PDF. (g) 5Y and All are read through the same 1,000-row ledger window as 1Y, so a longer history under-reports and All's span starts at the oldest row read. (h) The aurora is literal hex in `wallet-tokens.css` by the owner's own commit, and the commented-out dark overrides stay retired except the sheet shadow. REFINES Decision #123.** At the product owner's direction. **(A) The drawer is deleted** (`FinanceDrawer`, `wallet-drawer.css`, the drawer→dialog hand-off and its focus race) and its content is a `WalletLane` island on every `/wallet*` route (`walletLaneFor`, composed into `laneFor`): the wallet's page links as real addresses, the verification gate, and every offered money action as an icon grid, with the standard collapsed icon rail. Only the overview and analytics draw it. Measured at 1440: ruler and tools both at y=60, the ruler still at y=60 with the sheet scrolled 700px under it, and the ruler — not the sheet — at the hit-test point; 390: ruler 16–270, tools 283–374, no overlap. **(D) Pages**: `/wallet/transactions` (the full paged ledger + CSV), `/wallet/analytics` (cash flow, the balance breakdown, and new server-share breakdowns by category and by project), `/wallet/invoices` (the extracted `InvoicesPanel`, read server-side; a non-business wallet is told it is not billed, and the lane lists the page only for a business vault) — each under a compact hero naming the page. The overview keeps its sections but previews six ledger lines with "View all" and links Cash flow to Analytics; the invoices DIALOG is gone. `activity` now 308s to `/wallet/analytics`. Below 767px the lane's links and gate move to the top of the sheet (a strip), never drawn twice. **Verified** in a browser against the live local stack as Kwame (personal) and Priya (business vault), 1440 and 390, light + dark, `dir="rtl"` (lane, tools and ruler mirror; thumb on the checked cell; zero horizontal overflow), ruler clicks updating `?flow=` and the section heading, the 308, zero console errors; `deno task check` exit 0, lint clean, wallet tests 16/16 (2 new, for `walletPageHref` / `viewOfPath`). **FLAGGED — surface, do not silently resolve:** (a) every wallet page now does two overview reads per navigation (the lane's and the page's), because they are separate hydration roots and both must paint in the first byte; (b) sub-pages read the same payment data as the overview so their dialogs work — heavier than a ledger-only page needs; (c) the ruler's glass and the corner tools extend Decision #122's scoped glass exception (recorded in DESIGN_SYSTEM §B.4.3); (d) `/settings`, which the settings tool links to, is still a placeholder page; (e) `.claude/launch.json` was recreated with a `web-wallet` config (port 12974) that re-exports the `.env` service-role key, per the stale-machine-env note. | `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` §B.4.3 / top note · `ROUTING.md` · `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` §Sitemap · `apps/web/features/wallet/**` · `apps/web/routes/(dashboard)/{_layout.tsx,wallet/*}` · Decisions #63 / #122 / #123 |
| 125 | **Stripe fiat rails, Phase 1 — card payments into the ledger, Connect payout accounts, Identity KYC and the signed webhook (2026-09-29).** Projective stays the ledger of record; Stripe is only the card and payout rail. **(A) SEPARATE CHARGES & TRANSFERS, NOT DESTINATION CHARGES — a conflict with the brief and with the prior `SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md` blueprint, flagged here rather than silently resolved.** Both named Destination Charges while describing money HELD by the platform and released later. A destination charge transfers to the connected account the moment the payment succeeds, names exactly one destination at charge time and cannot hold escrow — while a stage's payee may not exist when it is funded, a team payout splits across several people (`fn_split_team_payout`), and every escrow in this schema is held FROM a wallet by `projects.fund_stage`. So the card is charged on the PLATFORM account (a `transfer_group`, no `transfer_data` / `on_behalf_of` / `application_fee_amount`), the settled amount becomes an ordinary `topup` credit, and an escrow lock holds the stage from that wallet through the existing `fund_stage` — one escrow engine, not a card-specific second one; payouts leave later as Transfers to an Accounts v2 Express recipient. The blueprint was rewritten accordingly. **CONFIRMED by the product owner 2026-09-29** — Separate Charges & Transfers is the pattern. **(B) SCHEMA, folded in place (§1)** — the brief asked for new additive migrations; §1 governs, so there is no ALTER-on-top file, and no column or FK of `finance.escrows` / `wallets` / `transactions` was touched. New enum `finance.inbound_payment_status`; new table `finance.inbound_payments` (one row per attempt — the twin of `finance.payouts`, needed because `transactions` records only completed movements, so a started or declined payment had nowhere to live) with seven CHECKs; `finance.payout_accounts` edited in place (the five-value owner axis, a status vocabulary equal to what the v2 `stripe_transfers` capability can report, `updated_at`, one active account per owner); an `org.freelancer_profiles.kyc_tier` CHECK (1–3); six indexes including one-row-per-processor-id guards on chargebacks, payouts and verification cases; the `identity_sessions_per_day` param (5); and one new category-1 file, `00001230_functions_finance_stripe.sql`, with 18 definer functions. **(C) TWO DOORS.** User doors (`EXECUTE` → `authenticated`, authorised through `auth.uid()`) open, bind or abandon an attempt and can never say money arrived; processor doors (`EXECUTE` → `service_role` only, explicitly revoked from `authenticated`) apply only what the signature-verified webhook reports; the four internal helpers are executable by no role. An `escrow_lock` amount is NEVER the client's: it is recomputed as the sum `fund_stage` escrows by, and the client's figure is only a check (`PC409` when the stage was re-priced). Settlement runs `fund_stage` AS the payer who authorised it (`request.jwt.claim.sub` = `created_by`), in a subtransaction, so a lock refused at settlement rolls back only the lock and the money stays in the wallet with `lock_error`. Every money-moving call registers a key in `finance.idempotency_keys` AND sends the same key as Stripe's `Idempotency-Key` (`projective:<op>:<id>`); every webhook event is claimed as `stripe:<evt_id>` in the same transaction as its effect. Zero PII: only provider ids and Stripe's own codes are stored. **(D) SERVICES AND ROUTES.** Fat `PaymentBackendService` (`@server/services/finance/`) over `live-payments.ts` (the DB doors), `stripe-rails.ts` (SDK calls from pure parameter builders) and `stripe-webhook.ts` (a pure `planStripeEvent` + dispatch); `packages/backend/core/stripe.ts` (lazy typed config that validates key SHAPE — a placeholder counts as absent — API version `2026-08-26.dahlia` pinned, fetch client, `constructEventAsync` over SubtleCrypto); seven thin routes under `/api/finance/` (`escrow/intent`, `topup/intent`, `connect/{onboarding,refresh,return,status}`, `identity/session`) plus the signed `webhooks/stripe` (raw body, 1 MiB cap, `no-store`, 400 on a bad signature, a livemode mismatch ignored). Zod SSOT `@projective/types/finance/payments.ts`; the finance Zod types were also brought back into line with the tables they mirror (`approve_spend` on `VaultCapability`, nullable `capCents` / `perTransactionCents`, `approvalThresholdCents`, `fundState`, `held`, a signed `amountCents` on subscription events, the five-value `FinanceOwnerType` on methods and billing). **(E) ENV AND A TRACKED-SECRETS FINDING.** `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` / `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, plus a NEW development-only `STRIPE_API_BASE` (stripe-mock; honoured only with a test key and never under `DENO_ENV=production`). The rails are live only with `FINANCE_BACKEND_LIVE=true` AND a well-formed key; otherwise every Stripe route answers 503. **Found while documenting where the keys go:** `.env`, `.env.development` and `.env.production` are TRACKED by git again despite Decision #11 and `.gitignore` (an ignore rule does not apply to a tracked file), and `apps/web/main.ts` loads only `.env.local` then `.env` — so a key written to `.env.development`, as `.env.example`'s header used to advise, is both inert AND committed by the next `git add`. | 128 | **Project requests, the hiring handshake, inbox folders, the conversation context panel and safe link previews (2026-10-01). REFINES Decision #116(B) — the intro a client WROTE is now also posted as their own DM message — and #113 — the cooldown refusal names the instant it lifts.** One brief, eight coupled deliverables. **(A) INBOX FOLDERS, folded in place (§1).** `comms.dm_participants.inbox_folder` (`primary` · `requests` · `archived`, CHECK-constrained) on the PARTICIPANT row, because the two people in a DM file it independently; `is_archived` becomes `GENERATED (inbox_folder = 'archived')` so the folder and the old flag cannot disagree (the column is kept, not dropped); indexes `(user_id, inbox_folder)`, `(thread_id, user_id)` and `dm_messages (thread_id, created_at DESC)`. `comms.set_dm_inbox_folder` is the participant's own door (definer, own row only); `comms.fn_promote_thread_on_reply` (`BEFORE INSERT ON dm_messages`) moves the SENDER's own row `requests → primary` — replying is accepting — and touches nobody else's, so a requester's follow-ups can never pull a thread out of the recipient's Requests and a reply into an archived thread leaves it archived. The Zod twins (`InboxFolder`, `folderAfterSend`, `requestRouting`, `folderUnreadCounts`) are pinned to the SQL by `folders.test.ts`; every read projects `ConversationSummary.folder` and `?folder=` partitions the list. **(B) THE HIRING HANDSHAKE.** `comms.send_request_message(recipient, body, project)` posts a request's opening message into the pair's DM — and REFUSES (`42501`) unless an open invitation or a pending application on that project stands between the two, so it is not a cold-message door; only when it OPENS the thread (created, empty, or restored from the recipient's deletion) does it file it — the recipient's row in `requests` unless the two follow each other, the sender's in `primary`; an existing conversation is never re-filed. The projects service calls it after the request is recorded: `hire` posts the client's intro (none written → no thread, so nothing is ever posted that the client did not write — the principle #116(B) protected); the new `projects.apply_to_project` (stage · optional staffing role · cover note; refusals for the owner's own project, an unlisted-or-inactive project, no freelancer profile, a person already on the stage and a second pending application per target) records a `pending` application ("Awaiting approval"), notifies the owner (`application.received`, an existing catalog event) and posts the note into the owner's Requests; `projects.respond_to_project_invitation` is finally reached by an application surface — `POST /api/projects/invites/respond` answers every invitation of one request together; `projects.assign_from_application` was rewritten to take any target (stage, role, open seat), refuse a non-pending application, fill a seat and mark its other pending applicants `rejected`, and notify `application.accepted`. `invite_to_project`'s cooldown refusal now carries `DETAIL = 'reopens_at=<ISO UTC>'`, surfaced by the fat service as `details.reopensAt` on its 422 (and the 10-per-10-minutes limit as `details.retryAt` on its 429) — `ServiceResult` gained an optional `details` record for exactly this. **(C) THE CONTACT FILTER COVERS DMs.** `comms.tg_mask_dm_message_pii` applies `comms.mask_pii` to a DM between two people negotiating or working on a protected project (an open or accepted invitation or application between them, or a protected project both are engaged in — `projects.fn_engaged_projects`), writing `pii_masked` / `pii_categories`; `invite_to_project` masks the intro the same way and the stub path mirrors both with `maskPii` (`packages/types/comms/pii.ts`, pinned to the SQL patterns by `pii.contract.test.ts`). The helper functions are executable by no client role. **(D) THE CONTEXT PANEL.** `projects.get_engagement_context(counterpart)` (definer; only rows the caller is a party to) feeds `MessagingBackendService.context`, whose `context-model.ts` DERIVES the rig server-side: a freelancer gets Accept request / Decline for every pending invitation of the latest request; a client gets "Fund escrow & confirm seat" for a pending applicant (POST accept, then the fund page) or for a confirmed seat awaiting funding. From 1280px the panel stands in the flow, sticky between the header and footer bands (the composer's band is MEASURED, because it grows), collapsible from a Details toggle remembered per viewer; below 1280px it is a right `Drawer`. **(E) THE INBOX LANE.** Folder tabs (`LaneTabs` gained a `dot` + spoken `hint`, and arrow/Home/End roving per the ARIA tabs pattern); rows end in a 48px slot whose compact time (`lastActivityShort`: now/5m/3h/2d/4w/1y) and unread dot hand over to a horizontal `…` on hover/focus/open by opacity alone; coarse pointers keep the menu visible; the row's link stretches over the row; one `ConversationMenu` serves the lane and phone rows, and folder moves are optimistic with rollback (`folder-moves.ts`). "New message" and "Create project" now share the new `LaneCreateButton` (`.proj-lane__create*` deleted). `Ctrl`/`Cmd+B` toggles the global rail except while typing (`shortcuts.ts`); the composer takes focus on arrival on a fine pointer only. **(F) LINKS.** The link scanner's live path is built (`link-guards` · `link-fetch` · `link-reputation` · `link-favicon` · `link-html`): DNS first with every answer checked (rebinding), the checked address pinned and TLS started against the hostname, redirects re-validated (max 2), a 5 s deadline, a stream-enforced 512 KiB cap, Google Safe Browsing (`LINK_SAFETY_API_KEY`), favicons re-hosted — all still behind `FILES_BACKEND_LIVE`. `LinkPreviewBackendService` turns a message's links into cards (internal: profile, project, listing, read under the reader's identity; external: the verdict, metadata only when `safe`); the bubble renders fixed-shape rows so a verdict never moves the feed, and any external link not known safe goes through the new `/exit` interstitial, which never redirects, needs an explicit "I understand" for anything unchecked or suspicious, offers no way on for a blocked link, and never lets a guest trigger a scan (a guest sees a remembered verdict plus the URL's own shape). `exit` is a reserved handle (TS + `org.fn_is_reserved_handle`). **(G) THREE DEFECTS FOUND BY MEASUREMENT, ALL MINE:** (1) the stub context read `Date.now()` while the conversation corpus is frozen at 17 Jul 2026, so every fixture invitation had "expired" and the rig rendered nothing — the stub now dates everything against `CORPUS_NOW`; (2) the warning badge as the filled `--warning` / `--on-warning` pair measured **3.2:1** at 12px in light mode — it is now a solid warning tint with `--on-surface` text, **11.2:1**; (3) adding `exit` to `RESERVED_HANDLES` without its SQL twin failed `workspace.contract.test.ts` until the migration list was edited. **VERIFIED BY EXECUTION:** every new RPC, trigger and grant inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` as real roles (routing with and without a mutual follow, no re-filing, restore, reply promotion for the sender only, the folder door's refusals, the cold-message refusal, apply/accept/seat-reject, the cooldown DETAIL, masking in a protected pair's DM and none in an unrelated one); in a driven headless Chromium on `deno task dev:mock`: the tabs and the Requests dot ("Requests, 1 unread" spoken), the row unchanged at 244×62 through the hover swap, a 48px slot and a 24px menu, Move to Primary moving the row and the dot, Ctrl+B toggling and inert in a field and in the composer, the coarse-pointer row (menu beneath the time, no overlap), the composer focused on a fine pointer and not on touch, the panel sticky at 96px and sized to the measured 90px footer, the toggle widening the chat 776 → 1096px, the 384px drawer at 1100px with Escape, Accept request → Accepted and the thread in Primary, safe links direct and flagged ones through `/exit`, every `/exit` state (blocked, suspicious, unchecked, internal path collapse `//evil.com` → `/evil.com`, a `javascript:` refusal at 422) with `noindex` + `no-referrer`, and the no-JavaScript consent round trip. `deno task check` 0 errors, `deno task lint` clean (1,848 files), **1,799 unit tests** with only the four pre-existing `theme-engine` failures (#96(a)). **No new Dev Context axis (§5)**: folders, requests and verdicts are server data, and pointer precision is a device capability the browser's own emulation already simulates. **FLAGGED — surface, do not silently resolve:** (a) the brief says a reply "moves the thread to Primary"; folders are per participant, so it moves the REPLIER's copy — a requester's follow-up never promotes the recipient's; (b) Archived is a third folder tab — the brief named Primary and Requests, but archive is a folder in the data model and the old All/Starred/Archived partition would have contradicted it; (c) the brief asked for an unread BADGE on Requests; the lane renders a dot with the count spoken, because §D.1 and `LaneTabs` forbid printed counts in lane chrome; (d) applications notify through the existing `application.received` event, not `stage.invite` as the brief wrote — the catalog already had the dedicated event, with its own digest window; (e) "Decline / Block" is rendered "Decline": there is no block feature, and the 48-day lockout is the only block that exists (per project) — a person-level block would be new product; (f) "Fund escrow & confirm seat" lands on `/wallet#upcoming` (or the project, for a seat parked at `pending_funding`) because no per-stage funding deep link exists; (g) the brief specified in-flow from 1280px and a drawer below 1024px; 1024–1279px uses the drawer too; (h) Safe Browsing's Lookup API sends the full URL to Google (the Update API would send hash prefixes only) — a privacy trade-off for a human; (i) `projective.io` / `www.projective.io` are ASSUMED to be the product's canonical hosts (`CANONICAL_HOSTS`); (j) the Explore "Apply to project" control is still the pre-existing client stub — the endpoint exists, the stage/role/cover-note picker does not; (k) the local database was NOT migrated: `deno task db:reset` rebuilds with these edited migrations but wipes local data (it holds the owner's own account and projects), so it needs the owner's go-ahead; (l) the phone inbox's row menu was `display: none` below 768px — phones had no row actions at all; it is now visible on coarse pointers; (m) the theme engine's filled `--warning` pair failing 4.5:1 in light mode is pre-existing and touches gate 12 — worth a human look beyond this badge. (2) THE PERSON'S RUNG: a person is metered as `user` but earns Standing as `freelancer`, and no recompute writes a `user` row, so `fn_subject_standing_level('user', …)` pinned every individual at rung 1 and the weekly bonus (+10…+40) never applied. `user` now reads the freelancer rung — which also corrects any other standing-scaled entitlement resolved for a person. **(D) TEAM APPLICATIONS.** `projects.apply_to_project(…, p_team_id)` applies on a team's behalf: the caller must hold `bind_seat` (`org.is_team_lead`), the team needs two active members, and it may not apply to its own project; the duplicate and already-on-stage checks are applicant-aware, so a lead may hold one pending application as themselves and one for the team. So the action reads "Withdraw proposal (refunds 1 proposal)", not the brief's "1 token". `projects.list_my_applications(p_project)` backs the sent list (`GET /api/projects/applications/mine`); `POST /api/projects/applications/withdraw` is the write. **(F) THE SURFACES.** The popover's meter sits under the completion block for anyone who sends proposals (a freelancer, or a team context): `Proposals: W/G weekly · B/C ready` (the buffer as units of CAP — `12/12` — where the brief's example showed the drip, `3/3`), a refill line, a portal tooltip naming the drip and the earned bonus, and `Accelerate volume with Pro →` at ≤ 5 weekly or an empty buffer on a free plan. All four read one client store (`proposals/core/allowance-state.ts`), so an application or a withdrawal moves every meter on the page with no reload, and every countdown runs on the SERVER's clock (the skew is carried with the status). **(G) DEV AXIS.** `proposalAllowance` (auto · healthy · low · paced · paced (unenforced) · week spent · team < 2) substitutes the STATUS client-side; the server gate is untouched. **FLAGS for a human:** (a) `/settings/billing` holds saved cards only — no plan can be bought there yet, so the upgrade link lands where Pro is not on sale. (b) The seed note on `team_free` says a free team "draws on its members' allowances rather than a dedicated pool", but the trigger meters a dedicated 50/week team pool, as the brief describes — the seed note or the trigger must change. (c) The modal defaults to "Yourself" even in a team context. (d) The enforced 422 path is pinned by unit tests of the rule and the gate's code path, not end to end — flipping `proposal_allowance_enforced` on the shared database is the owner's call. | 157 | **The global Accent Amber pair and the Button Interaction Matrix — one amber seed becomes `--accent` / `--on-accent` for every terminal financial / conversion commit, buttons are tiered by what they commit the person to, and translucent primary washes leave active rails, middle-nav lists and tags (2026-10-09). AMENDS Decision #153 (the checkout's private commit pair is retired for the global one; #70's pill unchanged) and DESIGN_SYSTEM §B.8.1 / §B.8.2 (the matrix; the one sanctioned two-fill rig becomes hue-ranked amber + monochrome) / §D.7.7 (the profile rig: Hire amber, Add to project monochrome); EXTENDS §A.1 / §A.2 / §B.4.2 / §B.11 / §B.12 / Part E 8.** At the product owner's direction (the "Accent Amber" directive). This entry is PHASE 1, the contracts; the engine, the `accent` severity, the checkout and profile migrations follow and land against them (PHASES 2–4, below). **(A) THE TOKEN.** `ACCENT_SEED = #D98216` → `CorePalette.of(seed).a1` (`A`); the ink comes from the BRAND seed's `n1` (`N`), the palette `--surface` / `--on-surface` resolve from. Light `--accent = A.tone(62)` = `#d88115` (≈ the seed) on `--on-accent = N.tone(10)` = `#191c1d` (= light `--on-surface`) — **5.77:1**; dark, the tonal lift, `A.tone(66)` = `#e58b22` (≈ `#E58A18`) on `N.tone(4)` (= dark `--surface`) — **7.39:1**, meeting the ≥ 7:1 dark rule. **(B) HIGH CONTRAST AND FIXED POLARITY.** The pair widens by `HC_DELTA` (12): the INK always moves away from the fill, `max(0, t − 12)` in BOTH modes (light 10 → 0, dark 4 → 0); the FILL moves up 12 in dark only (66 → 78 = `#ffb061`) and HOLDS at 62 in light, because raising it loses page visibility and lowering it closes the gap with the ink — light HC **7.07:1**, dark HC **11.63:1**; the pair never narrows. Polarity is fixed (light fill, dark ink, every mode) like `--primary` and unlike the mode-adaptive roles, so `fg()` / `on()` are bypassed: written `fg(62)` / `on(10)` the light branch converges to 50 over 22 under the overlay — the brand-pair trap of §A.1.1. **(C) THE PRESSURE POLE.** `--btn-shade` (`--on-surface`) is the accent's own ink side in light mode, so hover and press blend toward a mode-invariant near-white (`N.tone(100)`, what `--on-scrim` already resolves to) and label contrast RISES with pressure (§B.12.4) — #153's `--checkout-commit-pole` mechanism, promoted to the token layer. **(D) THE MATRIX (§B.8.1).** 1 · Terminal financial / conversion — `severity="accent"`, solid `--accent` / `--on-accent`, pill: every checkout commit (`.cko-commit` today), the profile hero's Hire, Fund Escrow. 2 · Primary structural commitment — monochrome inverted (`--btn-accent: var(--on-surface)`; `--btn-on: var(--surface)`, the §D.7.7 idiom): Add to project, primary creation triggers. 3 · Brand primary — solid `--primary` / mode-invariant `--on-primary`, reserved for major navigation active states and core workflow commits (Save photo, Attach Selected). 4 · Neutral outlined — border `var(--hairline-strong)`, `--on-surface` ink, MANDATORY for utility actions (the asset picker's Upload, profile media upload). 5 · Ghost / bare — secondary toolbar tools, escape hatches. **(E) TWO FILLS.** Legal in one decision region ONLY when ranked by hue — amber terminal against monochrome structural, the profile rig; two fills of the same colour remain a finding, and the §B.8 gate now also refuses a fill from outside its tier. **(F) SURFACE POLICY (§B.4.2, §B.11.6).** Semi-transparent primary washes (`rgba(primary, .15)`, `color-mix(… var(--primary) …, transparent)`) are PROHIBITED on active navigation rails, middle-nav lists and tags; the active rail is `background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--on-surface)` with an optional 2px inline-start indicator reserved `transparent` at rest. **(G) THE GATE (§B.12.2, Part E 8).** `--accent` / `--on-accent` joins the machine-checked set on the full terms — ≥ 4.5:1 in all four mode/contrast states, ≥ 7:1 dark, never narrowing — pinned in `packages/ui/system/core/theme-engine.test.ts`, which also takes over from `checkout-commit-tokens.test.ts`. **(H) THE KNOB (§A.2).** The Colors knob has two seeds, `dsConfig.seed` and `dsConfig.accentSeed`, both live from the dev theme controls through `applyConfig` → `:root` `style.setProperty`. **FLAGGED — needs a human, do NOT silently resolve:** (a) **Commit and warning are one hue again — in BOTH modes.** Light `--accent` `#d88115` against light `--warning` `#ca8100` (engine warning seed `#F19C13`, `a1` tone 60) measures **1.06:1**; dark `--accent` `#e58b22` against dark `--warning` `#ed990d` (tone 70) measures **1.14:1**. "Commit" and "needs attention" read alike in either theme — the exact §B.8.3 failure #153 fixed. Recommend retuning the warning ramp or the accent hue; a human picks which. (b) **Under the house 3:1 fill floor on every light ground, and lower under pressure.** The light fill rests at **2.97 / 2.84 / 2.69 / 2.55 / 2.42:1** on `--surface` / `--bg` / `--surface-1` / `--surface-2` / `--surface-3`; hover and press toward the light pole (8% / 12%) take it to **2.71 / 2.59:1** on `--surface` and **2.21 / 2.11:1** on `--surface-3`, the worst case; high contrast changes none of these (the light fill holds at 62, surfaces never widen). The label carries identification, so WCAG 1.4.11 is not failed, and #153's amber had the same property, but it deviates from the §B.12 gate's 3:1 clause and waives §B.12.4's "do not shave a floor" rule; recorded in §A.1.2, §B.12.4 and the §B.12 gate as a deviation, not a precedent. The alternative for a human: give the light branch the brand's treatment (`--btn-mix-hover` / `--btn-mix-active: 100%` plus the border-channel hover) and keep the light pole for dark only. (c) **Warning seed drift (pre-existing).** DESIGN_SYSTEM §A.1 and PRODUCT_SPEC §Visual Identity list the warning seed as `#D98216`; the engine uses `#F19C13`. The accent now owns `#D98216`; the warning rows in BOTH documents carry a drift marker, the values are not changed. (d) **`--text-main` is not a token.** The directive named it; ink is `--on-surface` (see the `checkout-stepper.css` note), and the docs map one to the other. (e) **`--hairline-strong` is a border shorthand** (`1px solid var(--hairline-strong-color)`, `packages/ui/styles/index.css`), used as-is for tier 4 — recorded so it is not re-mixed or misused as a colour. (f) **The entity-view lane is not reconciled.** §D.7.2 item 3's money verbs (Buy now · Book session · Reserve seat · Fund Stage 1) are tier 1 by the matrix, but an amber primary beside the lane's teal Add to basket would be two fills that are not the amber + monochrome pair, and the matrix reserves teal for navigation and workflow commits, which a basket is neither. (g) **"Accent" vocabulary collides.** Prose elsewhere in DESIGN_SYSTEM uses "the accent" loosely for the brand teal (§B.6, §B.9, §B.11.4), and the components' internal pair is named `--btn-accent` / `--x-accent`; neither is the new global `--accent`. | 160 | **The showcase picker chooses many, frames each, and writes nothing until Save & Apply — the selection ceiling, Browse → Continue → Crop, the carousel, staged uploads, and the drawer's corner controls (2026-10-09).** EXTENDS Decisions #158 / #159 at the product owner's direction. **(A) SELECTION.** `MediaPickConfig` gains `max` and `positions`; `MediaSection` opens an EMPTY slot with every empty slot (the pressed one first), so the ceiling is the empty-slot count, and a filled slot's Replace with that one slot; the photo and group targets stay at one, where a second click REPLACES the choice instead of refusing. A chosen card or tray chip toggles off (`toggleSelection`); at the ceiling the other cards are blocked with "You have N empty slots — remove one to choose another." Selected cards hide `.fh-asset__flags` so the tick never sits on the privacy mark. Slot 1 still takes only a still: `assignSlots` moves the first still into it and refuses a selection with none. **(B) TWO STEPS — FOR MULTI-SELECT ONLY.** A single-pick target (the photo, a group photo, a showcase Replace) has no Continue: choosing a library card, dropping a file or using the sign-in picture goes straight to Crop, and Back there lets the choice go so the next click picks again (owner direction, same day). A multi-select Browse never advances by itself — not even when a drop fills the ceiling. Browse's footer is Cancel + **Continue (n)** (disabled with its reason on the LEFT, in the tray slot, at zero); Continue enters Crop, whose footer is **Back** + **Save & apply**. Each item keeps its own crop and description (`PickItem`; the working crop is committed on every switch). The tray marks the active item (`data-active`, `aria-current`) and a chip click frames that item; muted ghost chevrons flank the stage and cycle circularly (`cycleIndex`); the bar reads "name · 2 of 3". **(C) STAGED UNTIL SAVE.** A dropped or chosen device file becomes a `staged` candidate — an object URL plus its decoded size — and the sign-in picture a `signin` candidate previewed from the provider URL; neither touches the server until Save & Apply, which uploads each staged file through `/api/media/upload-*`, syncs the sign-in picture, carries the crop over to the size the server decoded (`rescale`), then hands the host library ids. Closing, cancelling or removing a choice revokes its object URL. **(D) PRESENTATION.** In the picker `.fx-card__meta` drops the reserved hover-date row and sits on `--card-gap` / `--card-gap-tight` (62 → 51px); the hub's grid keeps its 62px constant. `InspectPanel` (shared by the picker drawer and `/files`) moves Open in new tab beside Close and Download onto the preview's top-left as icon-only ghost `Button`s with tooltips and `.ui-hit` floors; Delete stays labelled. **(E) VERIFIED.** `deno task check` 0 errors; lint clean; `deno task test:unit` 2,534 passed, only the four `theme-engine.test.ts` failures (#96(a)); `media-pick.test.ts` covers toggle-on/off, the ceiling, single-slot replacement, circular indices and slot assignment. Browser, live stack, owner `chloewinters` (showcase restored to its empty seed afterwards): an empty slot opened "Add to your showcase" with a ceiling of 6 (3 once three were filled); Continue disabled at zero; two dropped files staged as `blob:` URLs with `files.items` unchanged (9); a library card selected, re-clicked off, and the ceiling blocked three cards with the notice; flags hidden on selected cards; Continue → Crop with two chevrons 8px from the stage, next ×3 = 1→2→3→1, previous from 1 → 3, a tray chip switched to item 2; a 1.46× crop survived switching away and back; still no write; Back → Browse → Continue; Save & apply wrote exactly 2 uploads + 3 renditions and filled slots 1, 2, 3; a staged file then Cancel wrote nothing; 390px: no overflow; `/files` drawer: header [Open in new tab, Close], Download 32px at (8, 8) on the preview. **FLAGGED — surface, do not silently resolve:** (a) a multi-slot save applies slots one by one — if one fails, the earlier slots stay applied (named in the editor's notice) and the picker stays open with the error; (b) a staged upload that succeeded before a later failure is now a library row, and a retry reuses it rather than re-uploading; (c) the reserved hover-date row is dropped in the picker only, so its cards no longer show the date — the drawer still does; (d) the inspect-drawer change applies to `/files` too, because the component is shared; (e) the Download disc on the preview is a solid `--surface` disc with `--elevation-low`, not a transparent ghost, because a ghost icon over a photograph has no contrast to promise; (f) the crop phase has two ways back (the bar's icon and the footer's Back); (g) selection order decides slot order apart from slot 1's still rule — there is no drag-to-reorder; (h) a staged file's size is the BROWSER's decode; | 161 | **The shell-free File Inspector and the streaming media proxy — `/inspect/[fileId]` opens one stored file full-window, with the canvas that suits it and a details panel, and reads its bytes only through `GET\|HEAD /api/media/proxy/[fileId]`, which streams private objects through the app after the existing read gate (2026-10-09).** At the product owner's direction; EXTENDS the files read gate (`objectFor`, `live-objects.ts`, unchanged) and the share-response rules of Decision #67; takes explicit, FLAGGED exceptions to Decision #88 (flag (a)), DESIGN_SYSTEM Part D / §D.6 (flag (b)), the middleware's "a route may only tighten" CSP rule and Decision #126 (flag (c)) and guardrails §3 (flag (d)). Decision #132 (chat media tiles → `fileObjectHref`) is unchanged. **(A) STREAMING PROXY.** `MediaBackendService.streamAsset(actor, fileId, request)` → `services/media/stream.ts` `streamAssetFor`; transport `core/storage-stream.ts` `fetchStoredObject` reads storage's INTERNAL origin with the service key (`/storage/v1/object/authenticated/…`, never the public URL, never a client-supplied path). A non-uuid id is a `404` with no database round trip; then the unchanged `objectFor(actor, id, { tier, share })` gate. `Range` / `If-Range` / `If-None-Match` / `If-Modified-Since` and the abort signal are forwarded; 200 / 206 / 304 pass through, 416 is bodiless with `content-range: bytes */<size>`, every other upstream status (storage's 400-for-missing included) is the same bodiless `404`; `HEAD` has no body. Headers are an ALLOWLIST: from storage only `content-length`, `content-range`, `accept-ranges`, `etag`, `last-modified`; the proxy's own `content-type` (an inline-safe type kept, `image/svg+xml` kept, text-like → `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, else `application/octet-stream`, never `text/html`), `content-disposition` (`inline` only when inline-safe and not `?download=1`; the display name as ASCII + RFC 5987 `filename*`, never the path), `content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` on everything not inline-safe, `cache-control: private, no-transform, max-age=3600` (`private, no-store` for a share read) + `vary: cookie`, `nosniff`, `cross-origin-resource-policy: same-origin`, `x-robots-tag: noindex, nofollow`, `referrer-policy: no-referrer`; nothing names a host, bucket or path. A 1,200-a-minute sliding window keyed `s:<slug>` / `u:<user>` (anonymous public reads unkeyed) counts only fresh reads (no `Range`, or one from byte 0) → `429` + `retry-after`; storage unreachable → `503`; every refusal `no-store`. The `/api/files/object/[id]` redirect route stays for every other surface; the inspector uses only the proxy. `mediaProxyHref` / `MEDIA_PROXY_ROUTE` in `@projective/types/files` `inspect.ts`. **(B) PAGE ROUTE BY UUID.** `/inspect/[fileId]` (`fileInspectHref`, `INSPECT_ROUTE`) addresses a file by its `files.items.id` uuid, `?share=<slug>` optional. Controller `features/inspector/routes/InspectScreen.tsx` → `core/inspector-ssr.ts` → `FilesBackendService.inspect(id, { share }, actor)` (`live-inspect.ts`; pure `toInspectAsset` in `inspect-dto.ts`): `objectFor`'s three read branches, `source = 'supabase'` + `status = 'uploaded'` + not deleted, the canvas from the pure `resolveViewer(name, mime)` (extension first, stored type second; HEIC / TIFF / PSD draw their `lg` rendition or fall back), `access` owner · member · share · public, `canManage` / `shareUrl` / `downloadCount` server-derived and managers-only, the owner from `org.profiles_index`, and EVERY address a same-origin proxy or page route (`AssetItem.url` / `thumbnailUrl` are never carried). `InspectAssetSchema.safeParse` at runtime (mismatch → `503`); every refusal one calm `404` page that never says whether the file exists; `noindex, nofollow`, `no-referrer`, `private, no-store`. **(C) SHELL-FREE.** The page lives in a new route group `routes/(standalone)/` with NO `_layout.tsx` (only `_app.tsx`: tokens, a11y, `DevMount`) and a `_middleware.ts` that renews the session without redirecting (the `[handle]` model). The page owns its frame: a solid `--surface-1` top bar (mark → `/`, name, `--text-secondary` middot meta, Download, full screen, panel toggle), the canvas, and a details panel in a horizontal `Splitter` at `--bp-md`+ / a floating bottom sheet below it (open by default on desktop, persisted in `pj.local.inspector.panelOpen`; closed on mobile). **(D) PAGE-SCOPED CSP.** `apps/web/utils/csp.ts` gains `CspRelaxations` (`wasm`, `blobConnect`) and `cspHeaderFor(profile: "app" \| "inspector")`, cached per profile; the global middleware sends `cspHeaderFor("app")` (unchanged behaviour); only `/inspect/*` sends `inspector` = the app policy + `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` in `script-src` (pdf.js decoders, Draco / Basis / meshopt) + `blob:` in `connect-src` (GLB embedded textures), nothing else. `x-frame-options: DENY`, `object-src 'none'`, `frame-ancestors 'none'` still hold, so a PDF is drawn on a canvas, never framed. **(E) EXTERNAL ENGINES, THIS PAGE ONLY.** `three@0.186.0` (+ `@types/three`), `pdfjs-dist@6.3.289` (legacy build), `highlight.js@11.11.1`, `dompurify@3.4.15`, `docx-preview@0.3.7` (+ `jszip`), with `marked` already mapped — root `deno.json` `"$comment:inspector"`; engines only, never their CSS (pdf.js's text layer rules rewritten in tokens), reskinned with tokens; client-only, through a memoised dynamic `import()` inside an island effect (the `quill-loader.ts` pattern), never at module scope. | 163 | **The workspace Overview redesigned, a Task and a Session presented as one room, and review authority configuring the engagement (2026-10-10).** At the product owner's direction (the "Refactor Project Workspace Overview, Channel Topology, and Single-Task Navigation" brief), with three conflicts against logged decisions put to the owner and answered the same day. **(A) ONE ROOM, PRESENTED.** A Task or a Session presents exactly one shared room, named "Discussion" (`isSingleRoomEngagement`, `discussionRoomId`, `SINGLE_ROOM_NAME` in `detail.ts`): the File Explorer tree, the Overview's Messages list and the files index list that room (relabelled) and the viewer's private threads, never a stage room or the spare project-wide room. The stored topology is UNCHANGED — the owner chose presentation over a data-model change — so a Task's Discussion is still its root stage's room (#121(C), #133) and its project-wide room (#135) still exists, unlisted. **(B) THE TYPE-SWITCH SANITIZER.** `projects.sanitize_single_room_topology(project)` runs at the end of every live save that leaves the project a Task or a Session (and its stub twin trims the stored stages): a Task keeps its root stage (lowest `sort_order`) and retires every other stage with its rooms; a Session keeps its stages — they are its sessions — and retires their stage-bound rooms; the project-wide room is never touched. Retiring is a HARD delete only when the row carries no history at all (`fn_stage_has_history`: tickets current or required, ticket history, submissions, seats, open seats, invitations, invite links, every finance row, and room history; `fn_room_has_history`: messages, channel files, scheduled events) and otherwise an ARCHIVE — the owner's rule, which RESOLVES the conflict with guardrails §5 ("nothing is hard-deleted") for this path. New soft-removal columns `projects.project_stages.archived_at` and `comms.project_channels.archived_at`; the room SELECT policy hides an archived room (not `has_channel_access`, so its messages and files stay readable as history); the stage product reads (lane, board, overview, feed counts, members, submissions, setup, ticket commit, discussion resolution, wallet funding queue, personal calendar) filter it; `fn_enforce_structure_variation`, `set_project_status`, `approve_stage`'s handover check, `get_nav_activity` and `get_stage_channels` ignore it; `get_stage_channels` no longer provisions a Session's stage rooms. A save of a Task reconciles only its root stage, so a retired stage is never re-created against the one-stage cap. The two history probes are revoked from every client role. **(C) REVIEW AUTHORITY CONFIGURES.** `/details` (the editor; `/edit` stays #144's 308 to it) and `/preview` admit `projects.can_review_project` — the owner, or an active member of the paying client business — mirrored as `ProjectDetail.viewerCanConfigure` (`resolveReviewAuthority`, fail-closed) and `ResolvedProjectAccess.canConfigure` (a dev-simulated access overrides it); everyone else gets a 303 to `/projects/[slug]` — AMENDS #144, whose `/preview` sent a non-owner to the public listing. A business member is the client side, so their `viewerAccess` is `owner`. The write path widened to the same predicate: `projects.projects` UPDATE and a reviewer SELECT arm, `project_stages` and `stage_staffing_roles` FOR ALL, `project_attachments` SELECT/INSERT/DELETE, `stage_assignments` SELECT (so the onboarding lock sees the seats that freeze prices), and the owner checks inside `create_stage`, `delete_stage`, `reorder_stages` and `set_project_status` (messages keep "Only the project owner" for `refusalFrom`). `trg_guard_project_ownership` keeps `owner_user_id` and `client_business_id` the owner's alone. The stage Details tab and its guards read `viewerCanConfigure`. **(D) NAVIGATION.** A Task's top-tier "Details" view link is removed (REVERSES the Task half of the #121 view-link rule); every type's way into the configuration is the lane footer's icon-only "Edit project" control, for review authority only, drawn as a solid `--primary` / `--on-primary` fill while `/details` is open (`LaneIconButton` `fillWhenActive`, `.ui-lane-iconbtn--fill-active`; the collapsed rail's `.proj-railbtn--edit` likewise). The Overview hero's owner identity row (`.pjd-hero__identity`) is removed. **(E) THE OVERVIEW.** Main column: Needs you · Brief (description as prose; format · deadline · budget model as a middot line; skills as middot text, never tags — §B.11) · Inclusions & terms (a hairline ledger: NDA none / Projective standard / the client's own, IP ownership, portfolio, location, languages, deadline bonuses) · Project files (the client's reference files, searchable and filterable, previews through `/api/media/proxy/:fileId`; `ProjectAttachments` island) · the stage run · Recent updates. Aside: a participant's Active submissions (their own units by review state — in revision, pending review, approved) and Claimable tasks (`todo`, described, unclaimed, on a seated `open_pull` stage, within `max_concurrent_intensity` after the work they hold), Your work, Your earnings · Messages, hidden when it would list only the Discussion the lane already links · People (avatar, name, handle, Owner / Client member / Freelancer, stages except on a Task, hired team, role in the paying business — `ProjectMemberRow.team` / `.business`). The setup is now read for every viewer; only the composed brief reaches a participant, prices stay the owner's (`composeWorkspace`). FLAGS for a human: (a) **the SQL has not been through `db:reset`** — every changed migration parses (`@libpg-query/parser`, PL/pgSQL included) and a rolled-back probe on `prj-67o7d44y6x` passed (a client-business member converts, sanitizes: 2 stages + 2 rooms deleted, 1 stage archived; re-pointing the client business, a stranger's sanitize and a direct history-probe call all refused; a second sanitize is a no-op; the Task cap refuses a new stage); (b) the brief's `.ui-nav-item__dot` does not exist — `NavItem`'s `dot` prop renders no element despite its docblock — so the Overview keeps its pulsing `.pjd-dot`; (c) the brief's `in_revision` / `approved` / `ready` are the schema's `revision_requested` / `accepted` / `todo`, worded at the surface rather than renamed; (d) "one room" was applied to shared project rooms: private threads and a group session's cohort sub-groups (#48) are still listed; (e) the sanitizer keeps a Session's stages (deleting them would delete its sessions) — the brief said "stages and channels"; (f) the history test counts any seat, invitation or finance row, so most real extra stages will archive rather than delete; (g) ~90 definer and label reads (finance labels, profiles, search, explore) still see archived stages — classified as history, not filtered; (h) `files.fn_can_read` still has no project-attachment arm, so a client's privately stored reference file stays hidden from freelancers in Project files (needs the attachment INSERT policy tightened first, flagged earlier the same day); | 165 | **The work-start gate: no hold, no work — a freelancer may claim or start a ticket only once its escrow is held; a refused hold refuses the claim and moves the ticket to Needs funding (2026-10-10). Product-owner ruling, decision only — no code in this change.** **(A) THE SKIP BECOMES A REFUSAL.** `finance.fn_hold_ticket_escrow` (`00001200_functions_finance_core.sql`) today returns NULL and lets the claim succeed when there is no price, no payee, no payer wallet in the project's currency, or an INDIVIDUAL payer cannot cover the hold (a business that cannot cover it already refuses through `fn_wallet_debit`, and the spending-limit check already raises). The "already held" early return is not a skip and is unchanged. **(B) LOCK TRIGGERS** follow PRODUCT_SPEC §Escrow, Wallets & Finance #2: One-Off / Task upfront (when the project or first stage begins — its seat is hired by then), Pipeline at **claim** (§Escrow Lifecycle for Tickets is authoritative; the #2 table's "In Progress" wording is amended to say so), Sessions at booking. **(C) THE STATE MACHINE** `Draft → Needs funding → Payment processing → Funded → In progress → In review → Released`, `Failed` (retryable) and `Refunded` (terminal per escrow), with who acts and what unlocks each step, is written to `PRODUCT_MANAGEMENT.md` §3.6 as a §3.5 domain lifecycle — never a board column. **(D) `finance.escrows.payer_business_id` IS NULLABLE** — checked against `00000017_tables_finance.sql`: since Decision #126 (2026-09-29) the column has no NOT NULL and `ck_escrows_one_payer` requires exactly one of `payer_business_id` / `payer_user_id`, which is what lets `fn_hold_ticket_escrow` hold for an individual client. | 172 | **Business auto-funding, the low-balance warning, the monthly invoice run and paying on account (2026-10-10). Product-owner ruling on four questions put in chat the same day, then built.** PRODUCT_SPEC §Escrow, Wallets & Finance #4 gains Auto-funding, the Low-balance warning, What an invoice asks for and Paying on account; before this they existed only as the words "low balance" in `finance-model.md` §15's notification list. **(A) FROM WALLET IS A QUEUE, NOT A RETRY.** A ticket enters Needs funding only after a hold from the business wallet was refused (no funds, the owner's spending limit, or no payee once the refused claim is rolled back), so a From-wallet hold tried at that instant always fails. Ruling: the ticket joins the business's auto-fund queue (no storage — the Needs-funding tickets of `from_wallet` projects) and every credit to the wallet except an on-account credit retries it, oldest ticket first (`finance.fn_auto_fund_drain`, fired by `trg_transactions_wallet_watch`). A ticket with a payee is held as the project owner (`escrows.auto_funded`); one without returns to Draft so its next claim holds. Holds stay inside the owner's spending limit; at or above the wallet's approval threshold an owner without `approve_spend` gets a spend approval and `decide_spend_approval` retries the queue on approve. `add_to_basket` writes the business's default-basket line in SQL — the same row `BasketBackendService.addTicket` writes — because the refusal happens inside a freelancer's claim, where the owner's basket session is not reachable. Mode on `org.business_profiles.auto_fund_mode`, override on `projects.auto_fund_override`. **(B) THE INVOICE TOTAL IS ESCROW + BONUS + TAX.** The brief asked for the total to include the fee; the platform fee is deducted from the payee at release (`fn_release_ticket_escrow`), so adding it would bill it twice. The fee is a line shown as included. `fn_generate_consolidated_invoice` now selects by the new `escrows.released_at`, issues one invoice per currency with the platform as issuer (`issue_from_profile` NULL, relaxed in place), sets `due_date` (`invoice_due_days` = 14) and `amount_due_cents`, is idempotent on `uq_invoices_business_period_currency`, and notifies `invoice.issued`. **(C) PAYING ON ACCOUNT: THE PLATFORM FRONTS A WALLET CREDIT.** Wallet-funded escrow is already paid, so an invoice owes only what was bought on account. Checkout's Invoice route (`finance.place_on_account_order`) credits the business wallet (`on_account_credit`) and places the wallet order in one transaction, so every hold still comes from a wallet (#165 rule 2); KYB-verified, monthly invoicing, nothing overdue, owed ≤ `on_account_limit_cents` (25,000.00 per currency, product-owner figure). Pay = `finance.pay_invoice` (`invoice_payment` debit). **(D) THE RUN** is `finance.fn_run_billing_cycle` on pg_cron daily 02:20 UTC: each monthly business's last closed period (a missed day catches up), last month's statements for every wallet (`finance.fn_generate_statement`, balances derived from sums), and the overdue sweep (`invoice.overdue`). **(E) LOW BALANCE** is `low_balance_floor_cents` on the default-currency wallet; the debit that crosses it warns `add_funds` holders once (read off the debit itself, so it re-arms on recovery) and runs any `below_floor` deposit rule (`finance.deposit_interval` edited in place); the queue outgrowing the balance warns once too. **(F) CHECKOUT** — `checkout-model.ts` and `PaymentChoice.tsx` said Invoice is never a per-purchase instrument; | 173 | **The notification UI — the header drawer and `/notifications` read the real inbox, and live updates come from POLLING `/api/notifications/summary`, not a Realtime socket or an SSE route (2026-10-11).** **(A) THE CHOICE.** The brief offered a server-mediated SSE route (`GET /api/notifications/stream`, Supabase Realtime held server-side) or polling the summary, and asked for one with a reason. **Polling wins:** (1) it works identically under `deno task dev:mock` (fixtures have no Realtime) and live, so the one code path is the tested one; (2) an SSE route would hold one server-side Realtime socket per open tab, bound to an access token that expires mid-stream and must be re-minted inside a long-lived response — a session-refresh path nothing else in the app has; (3) the summary is one `SECURITY INVOKER` RPC over an indexed own-row read, so a 30 s cadence per VISIBLE tab (paused while hidden, immediate on return) costs little; (4) nothing in the inbox is latency-critical — chat has its own live channel (Decision #49), and a notification that lands within 30 s meets the product need. Islands stay free of Supabase either way. **(B) ONE POLLER PER PAGE.** `NotificationDrawer` (always mounted by `UserActions`) runs it and publishes the summary on a shared signal (`notification-state`); the header dot (`unseen > 0`, a dot never a count — DESIGN_SYSTEM §D.1) and the tab counts read it. | 178 | **Personalised discovery ranking — one quality score behind every "recommended" order (a cold-start prior · workload against the Global Intensity Cap · the newcomer Discovery Boost · Standing's multiplier · the trust penalty, every coefficient from `search.search_weights`), the anon-cached catalogue plus a viewer-scoped pass under the viewer's own JWT, `org.recent_views`, and the Home's "Because you viewed" / "Saved" / Trending rails (2026-10-12).** **(A) THE SCORE** (`packages/backend/services/explore/ranking.ts`, pure, 12 tests). `total = standing × (sentiment + volume + availability + boost) + penalty`: sentiment is the item's rating shrunk toward its track's corpus mean by 5 pseudo-reviews (a newcomer starts at the average, one 5★ cannot outrank fifty 4.9★s) × `review_sentiment`; volume saturates logarithmically at 50 reviews × `review_count`; availability is the free share of the owner's cap × `workload` (zero AT the cap — the spec's Discovery Loop); the Boost (`discovery_boost`, NEW seed row, 1.25) needs utilisation 0, no penalty, no rating under 4.0, and joined ≤ 90 days OR still on rung 1; Standing's `discovery_weight_bp` scales the earned terms; `discovery_penalty` (≤ 10) subtracts unscaled × `penalty`. The catalogue is assembled best-first and `getResults` / `rankRecommended` / the Home lists read `catalog.scoreById` (`compareRecommended` without scores keeps the handed order, so the typeahead's tie-break needed no change). **Verification is no longer a ranking term** — the old comparator put verified owners first, contradicting PRODUCT_SPEC §Reputation & Discovery 5 / #155 ("no discovery boost is attached to verification; discovery weight comes from Standing alone"); PRODUCT_SPEC wins, so this corrects code drift rather than a doc conflict. A project speaks with its CLIENT's reviews and carries the worse of its poster's and client business's penalty ("their project posts are de-ranked"). **(B) TWO PASSES.** The shared pass stays one anon read cached 30 s and adds three public-by-construction signals: penalised rows of `search.profiles_index`, `search.ranking_weights()` (a definer projecting key · weight · is_active only) and `search.trending_entities()` (distinct people per entity over 7 days — views 1, saves 2 — floored at THREE people so no row traces to one person's history). The viewer pass (`viewer-signals.ts`) reads `org.recent_views`, `org.user_bookmarks`, `search.user_affinity` (decayed, 14-day half-life) and `users_public.interests` + the seller's own skills with `getUserClient(jwt)`, per request, never cached; a failure is logged and the shared feed is served. `/explore` renews a lapsed session in place (the `[handle]` middleware's move) so a returning reader is not served a guest's Home; `landing()` stays shared. **(C) SCHEMA.** `org.recent_views` (00000011: one row per person per entity, `view_count`, `first_viewed_at` / `viewed_at`, CHECK vocabulary = `org.bookmark_entity_type` + product · article · user), read-own + clear-own policies only (00002010), INSERT/UPDATE revoked and nothing for `anon` (00002520), two indexes + two bookmark indexes (00004001); its one writer is `search.record_view` (00001400, definer, `auth.uid()` never a parameter, server-stamped times — a client-written future `viewed_at` would pin an item in Trending — topic affinity bumped with the same decay; EXECUTE revoked from `anon`, 00002510). `org.profiles_index` appends `discovery_weight_bp` and `workload_cap` (the person's `max_workload_intensity`, else `global_workload_cap_default`; a team's = its active members' defaults combined). Zod: `@projective/types/explore` `signals.ts`. **(D) RECORDING A VIEW** is server-side where the opening happens — `/view/[entity]`, `/[handle]/view/[item]`, `/[handle]` (fire-and-forget; a guest or a crawler records nothing; your own work is not recorded, so nobody nudges it toward Trending) — plus the results drawer's in-place open through `POST /api/explore/views` (a background beacon). **(E) THE RAILS** (`personalise.ts`, pure, 10 tests): "Because you viewed …" = the newest of the last three views with ≥ 3 same-family relatives (Jaccard over topics + skill families), excluding everything opened and the viewer's own; without one, "Picked for you" from decayed affinity, else stated interests + skills — briefs for a seller (the spec's Recommender Logic), services · products · talent for anyone else; "Saved" = bookmarks newest first; Trending past the floor, else "New on Projective" (published ≤ 30 days), else no rail.
