| 179 | **Voyage AI voyage-4 embeddings in discovery, behind `EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED` and a development-only switcher override — search re-ranking and the `/view` "Similar" rails (2026-10-12).** **(A) THE VENDOR.** Voyage AI `voyage-4`: 1024 dimensions, unit-length vectors, so inner product ranks exactly as cosine. Plain `fetch`, no SDK (`services/search/voyage-client.ts`): `input_type` always sent (`document` for listings, `query` for searches), `output_dimension: 1024`. Two hosts serve the same API and refuse each other's keys with a 403: MongoDB Atlas `https://ai.mongodb.com/v1/embeddings` (Atlas model API keys — the brief's endpoint and the default) and `https://api.voyageai.com/v1/embeddings` (Voyage platform keys, `pa-…`); the client picks the host from the key unless `VOYAGE_API_BASE` names one (see flag (a)). Limits checked against the Atlas API reference: 1,000 inputs and 320K tokens per request for voyage-4, 32K per text, a free-trial key held to 3 RPM / 10K TPM — so batches stay at ≤ 128 texts and ≈ 8K estimated tokens. Each call has a per-attempt timeout and an overall deadline (3 s for a query, 2 min for a backfill batch) and at most two retries with exponential backoff + jitter (or `Retry-After`) on 429 / 5xx / timeout / network, none on 400 / 401 / 403. The key goes into the `Authorization` header and nowhere else, and is scrubbed from any echoed error. **(B) THE DIMENSION CHANGE.** `vector(1536)` → `vector(1024)` on `search.profiles_index` · `projects_index` · `services_index` and `query_logs.query_embedding` (00000018, edited in place), each index table gaining `embedding_model` · `embedding_hash` (SHA-256 of the embedded text) · `embedded_at`, all nullable until the backfill; the HNSW indexes are rebuilt with `vector_ip_ops` (00004004). **(C) THE MOCK EMBEDDING IS GONE.** `search.fn_mock_embedding`, `fn_fill_mock_embedding` and the three `trg_fill_embedding_*` triggers (a hash-derived vector on every index row) are deleted (00001400 / 00001800 / 00002510); the `sync_*_to_index` triggers that keep `fts` stay. `fn_search_entities` and `fn_log_query` take a trailing nullable `p_query_embedding vector(1024)`: NULL scores the vector term 0 / stores NULL. **(D) COVERAGE: A NEW `search.catalogue_index`, NOT AN EXTENDED TABLE.** Of the five things `live-catalog.ts` loads, listings-as-services (`services_index`), public projects and listed profiles had index rows; products and articles had none. Extending `services_index` was ruled out — its key is `service_id REFERENCES marketplace.service_blueprints`, so a product or an article cannot be a row without dropping that FK (and §1 forbids reshaping it into a polymorphic key in passing); `projects_index` is project-keyed the same way. So one table keyed `(entity_type ∈ product · article, entity_id)` — the shape `profiles_index` already uses for four kinds — with `title` · `fts` · `is_public` · the embedding columns, kept by two new definer sync triggers (`sync_product_listing_to_index` on `catalogue.listings`: a product's title, description and status ride its LISTING; `sync_article_to_index` on `catalogue.articles`), visibility = the source is `published`, RLS "Public can view catalogue search index", backstopped in `seeds/09_search.sql`. Every one of the 49 public discovery entities in the seed world now has an index row. **(E) THE DOORS.** `search.fn_set_embedding(entity_type, entity_id, embedding, model, hash)` — definer, the only writer of the vectors, EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC / anon / authenticated and granted to `service_role` alone. `search.fn_nearest(p_embedding, p_types, p_exclude, p_limit)` — definer, `(entity_type, entity_id, score)` best first under each index's own anon visibility rule (the USING clause of its SELECT policy), so it answers nothing anon could not already read and never a vector. `search.fn_nearest_to_entity(…)` — the same, seeded with one PUBLIC entity's STORED vector read inside the database: the "Similar" rail needs the item's vector, and fetching it in the app would mean either a service-role read on a public page (the alternative #178(b) declined) or vectors on the wire. 00002520 takes back the table-level SELECT 00002500 gave `anon` / `authenticated` on the four index tables and `query_logs` and re-grants every column except `embedding` · `embedding_model` · `embedding_hash` · `embedded_at` (`query_embedding` on `query_logs`): a PostgREST select of them, or of `*`, is refused. Zod: `@projective/types/explore` `embeddings.ts`. **(F) THE SWITCH.** `EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED` (default false) in `core/env.ts`; `isEmbeddingsLive(req?)` in `core/supabase.ts` = not `USE_MOCKS` ∧ Supabase configured ∧ a real `VOYAGE_API_KEY` ∧ the effective setting, which is the env flag unless the request carries `pj.dev.embeddings` (`on` | `off`). The cookie counts only under `DENO_ENV=development` AND reaches the gate only from a development build (routes pass `IS_DEV ? req : undefined` — the `pj.dev.landing` guard), so production ignores it twice over; an override can turn the switch on but never without the key; callers without a request (writes, the backfill) get the environment's answer. The pure gate (`core/embeddings-gate.ts`) is unit-tested over the full env × cookie × dev/prod × key table. Dev Context Switcher (§5): an `embeddings` axis (Follow env · On · Off) in `DevOverrides` + `DEV_DEFAULTS` + `DEV_EMBEDDINGS`, the panel control, `reflect()` set / delete, the seam (`data-dev-embeddings`, `DevEmbeddings`), writing the cookie and reloading `/explore` and `/view/*`; the field's status line reads the effective state from the development-only `GET /api/explore/ranking` (404 in a production build). In development `/explore`, both `/view` page routes and every `/api/explore/*` response carry `x-discovery-ranking: semantic | heuristic` — what actually ordered that response, so a fallback reads heuristic. **(G) THE READ PATH.** Off: byte-for-byte the heuristic path — no Voyage call, no extra RPC, `fn_log_query` called with exactly its previous arguments. On, a search with a query embeds it (a process-wide LRU + TTL cache keyed by the normalised query, concurrent calls shared), asks `fn_nearest` for the category's kinds, and the pure `services/explore/semantic.ts` keeps every facet, the category and the JS candidate set, re-ranks the candidates on the default "recommended" sort by `(1 − SEMANTIC_BLEND_WEIGHT) × position + SEMANTIC_BLEND_WEIGHT × similarity` (weight 0.5; position 1 − i/n, similarity normalised to the best) and adds up to 12 neighbours the text match missed that clear max(0.30, 0.8 × the best) and pass the same facets — the floors measured on the seed world, where voyage-4 query-to-listing cosines run ≈ 0.34–0.42 for a match and ≈ 0.19–0.30 for an unrelated item. An explicit sort the reader picked still decides the order. The `/view` "Similar" rail takes the nearest same-type items to the item's stored vector, excluding the item and everything its owner published, topped up from the heuristic; no vector → the heuristic rail. Home personalisation and user vectors stay out (the ranking-v1 task): a `// #region` hook point in `ExploreBackendService.home` only. **(H) THE WRITE PATH.** `deno task embeddings:backfill [--dry-run] [--force]` reads the public catalogue as `anon`, builds each item's text (`core/embedding-text.ts`, pure and tested: type label · title · category · skills · summary, plus model and delivery for a service) and its hash, skips a matching hash + model, embeds in chunks and writes through `fn_set_embedding` with the service-role key; a rate limit or an outage waits and resumes, a refusal stops. `--dry-run` prints the count, a token estimate (≈ 4 characters a token) and the cost at $0.06 / 1M without calling Voyage. | 185 | **`/api/auth/verification-status` stops being an email-enumeration oracle; the `/verify` poll is bound to the browser that joined (2026-10-13).** **(A) THE DEFECT.** The route was unauthenticated, took `?email=`, and `AuthBackendService.getVerificationStatus` answered `{ verified }` from a service-role read of `org.user_emails` for that address, so anyone could learn whether an address had a confirmed account. `/api/auth/resend` and `/api/auth/forgot-password` already avoided this. The route JSDoc also claimed the poll "auto-logs the user in"; it never minted a session. **(B) THE BINDING.** `POST /api/auth/join` (individual email/password and enterprise owner), and a password sign-in that GoTrue refuses only for an unconfirmed email, set `pj_pending_verification`: HttpOnly, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/api/auth`, one hour (GoTrue's OTP lifetime), value `v1.<userId>.<expSeconds>.<base64url HMAC-SHA256>` (`packages/backend/core/pending-verification.ts`). The HMAC key is derived from `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` under a fixed label, so no new env key; with no service key no cookie is minted and every poll is uniform. The token travels on the `ServiceResult.pendingVerification` envelope field and `toAuthResponse` mints it, the same way `session` stays out of the JSON body. **(C) THE POLL.** `services/auth/verification-status.ts` `resolveVerificationStatus` (pure, injected deps): it takes no email (any `?email=` is ignored); it answers only for the cookie's user id, from GoTrue `email_confirmed_at` via `auth.admin.getUserById` rather than `org.user_emails` (an address can also be someone else's secondary). No cookie, a forged / foreign-key / swapped-id / expired cookie, and a still-pending account all get the identical `200 { verified: false }`. Every poll goes through a `SlidingWindowLimiter` (30 / 60s, keyed `pending:<id>` when the cookie is valid, else `client:<remote address>`; 429 with `retryAt`). A failed lookup is a 503, never a false pending. `cache-control: no-store`. **(D) THE UI.** A confirmed answer carries `signedIn` (whether the request holds `sb-access-token`). `true` continues in as before (OTP entered, or the link opened in this browser, which set the session). `false` (link opened on another device) shows `EmailConfirmedPanel` ("Email confirmed" + Sign in → `/login?notice=confirmed`, which shows a success banner) instead of navigating into a guarded route that bounced to `/login`. New dev axis `emailConfirmation` (Server · Pending · Confirmed · Signed in) substitutes the poll answer client-side, since the stub backend never confirms. **(E) TESTS.** `pending-verification.test.ts` (round trip, foreign key, swapped id, expiry, malformed), `verification-status.test.ts` (email-only caller, unbound = pending body, mismatched cookies, per-account and per-address rate limits, both success paths, 503), `verify-poll.test.ts`, `respond.test.ts`. Probe `supabase/probes/verification_status_oracle.ts` compares the answers for a seeded and an unknown address over HTTP. FLAGS (a) **pre-existing, not fixed here:** at HEAD `service_role` has no `USAGE` on schema `org` (`00002500` grants `org` to `anon`, `authenticated` only; `has_schema_privilege('service_role','org','USAGE')` is false on the shared DB), so every service-role `org.*` read fails. The old poll swallowed that error and answered `false`, which hid the oracle on the live stack (it would reopen the moment the grant lands). The same failure breaks username sign-in (`resolveUsernameEmail`) and this change's unconfirmed-sign-in user-id lookup (`resolveSignInUserId`, which then sets no cookie; the 6-digit code still works). A human should decide whether `service_role` gets `USAGE` on `org`. (b) The limiter is per process, like every limiter in `core/rate-limit.ts`. (c) The fallback key is `ctx.info.remoteAddr`, the proxy's address behind a reverse proxy; unbound callers learn nothing either way. (d) The cookie is not cleared on confirmation; it expires within the hour and only ever reveals its own account's state. (e) `documentation/architecture/MVP_FLOW_AUDIT.md`, cited by the task brief, does not exist in the repo. | `packages/backend/{core/pending-verification.ts,services/{ServiceResult.ts,auth/{AuthBackendService,verification-status}.ts}}` · `apps/web/{routes/api/auth/verification-status.ts,utils/{auth-cookies,dev-seam}.ts,features/auth/{core/{respond,AuthService,verify-poll}.ts,components/EmailConfirmedPanel.tsx,hooks/useVerifyPollSimulation.ts,islands/{VerifyForm,LoginForm}.island.tsx,types/mod.ts},features/devtools/{core/dev-context.ts,components/DevContextPanel.tsx}}` · `SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md` §Authentication · `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` §Authentication surfaces · `database/org/Tables.md` |
| 186 | **The ledger is append-only and reconciled nightly (2026-10-13).** MVP audit 3.3 / §2.5, work order M3. `finance.wallets.balance_cents` is a cache written beside `finance.transactions` by `fn_wallet_credit` / `fn_wallet_debit`; append-only was a convention held by grants (the service role held `GRANT ALL`), `wallet_id` was `ON DELETE CASCADE`, both primitives returned silently on a missing wallet, and nothing compared the cache with the ledger. No function updated or deleted ledger rows (grep), so there was nothing to refactor into compensating inserts; the two direct INSERTs in `simulate_wallet_transaction` are appends with consistent balances. **(B) RESTRICT.** `transactions.wallet_id` is `ON DELETE RESTRICT`, edited in place in `00000017`; no code path deletes a wallet. **(C) LOUD PRIMITIVES.** A missing wallet raises `PW404` from both primitives. Scheduled nightly at 03:40 UTC as the guarded pg_cron job `finance-reconcile-wallets` (R2 has not landed). The local DB reconciled cleanly at the time (22 wallets, zero drift). FLAGS (a) the scheduler is the guarded `cron.schedule` block, like `finance-billing-cycle`; R2 should adopt the job and make a skipped registration loud. (b) Drift lands in `ops.log_entries` (admin-readable) plus a WARNING, with no page or email; that table's future retention sweep may delete old rows (a persisting drift is re-reported nightly). A real alert channel is an ops follow-up. (c) `live-payments.ts` maps the new codes to a generic logged 500, but `wallet-actions.ts` maps unknown SQLSTATEs to 422 with the raw message, so an internal `PW404` sentence could reach a user if a future caller skips `fn_ensure_wallet`. (d) The primitives still match currency exactly (case-sensitive); all stored currencies are upper-case today, and a lower-case caller now raises instead of vanishing. (e) Beyond the brief: the service role's grant on `finance.transactions` is narrowed from `ALL` to `SELECT, INSERT`, so the grant no longer contradicts the trigger. A concurrent caller waits, re-reads the rows as `escrow_funded` and holds nothing (`P0001`, nothing fundable). Ticket locks always precede the payer's wallet-row lock, the same order `fund_ticket` (row lock, then hold) and a claim already follow; the auto-fund drain uses `SKIP LOCKED`. The index is the backstop for every other door. **(F) VERIFIED** on an isolated stack (HEAD plus only these edits, own `project_id`/ports): migrations and every seed apply under both indexes (the seed writes one escrow per ticket); the new `supabase/probes/escrow_uniqueness.sql` races two real transactions over `dblink` and passes, as do `paid_revisions`, `single_ticket_purchase`, `escrow_settlement_authority` and `cohort_session_isolation`. (c) The brief expected an existing escrow kind/revision column; there was none, so `revision_id` was added (additive, nullable). A database holding a pre-#189 revision escrow beside a held base escrow would refuse the index until that row's `revision_id` is backfilled; a consolidated `db:reset` never has one. And `POST /api/context/switch` / `POST /api/user/freelancer` left the claims stale for any caller other than those two clients. **(B) THE SPLIT.** `services/auth/refresh-outcome.ts` (`isRefreshRejection` / `refreshFailure`, tested against auth-js's own error classes): a refused grant — GoTrue `400`/`401`/`403` (`refresh_token_not_found`, `refresh_token_already_used`, `invalid_grant`, `user_banned`) or `AuthSessionMissingError` — is `401`; everything else (network, `5xx`, `429`, an unparseable body, a session-less success) is `503`. The refresh route clears the cookies on `401` only and answers `503` with them kept; `ensureSession` returns `clearCookies` only on `401` (the guard still bounces, but the session survives the outage); `apiFetch` routes to `/login` only when the refresh answered `401`, and hands the original `401` back on a `503`. **(C) SERVER RE-ISSUE.** Both mutation routes call `session.ts` `respondWithReissuedSession` after a successful service result: `renewSession` mints the rotated cookies onto the same response and the body carries `claimsStale: false`; a failed renewal keeps the old cookies and answers `claimsStale: true` (`WorkspaceResult.claimsStale`). A failed mutation never touches the session. **(D) CLIENTS.** `useContextSwitch` and `partner-service` drop their own `/api/auth/refresh` call, hard-navigate on success as before, and on `claimsStale` report and do not navigate (Decision #150's rule); both mutations are idempotent, so retrying re-issues again. AMENDS #46 (fail-closed now means refusal-only) and #150 (the client-side refresh step). Tests: `refresh-outcome.test.ts`, `apps/web/utils/session-reissue.test.ts`, `apps/web/utils/api-client.test.ts`. **(E) FOLLOW-UPS, BUILT THE SAME DAY (closing flags (b)–(d)).** (b) `BecomePartnerWizard`'s alert action was **Reload**, which re-mints nothing (a reload of a page whose access cookie is live never renews); it is now **Try again**, re-running the idempotent unlock, which re-issues the session. (c) The Settings writes re-issue server-side too: `POST /api/user/handle`, a `freelancer_profile` `POST`/`DELETE /api/user/lifecycle` (account deletion changes no claim), and a `PATCH /api/user/preferences` whose patch touches a claim (`touchesTokenClaims` in `@projective/types/org`: `locale`, `preferredDisplayCurrency`, `dateFormat` — the `CLAIM_PREFERENCE_KEYS` the hook stamps); `serviceBody` split out of `serviceResponse`. `SettingsService.renewSession` is deleted, `ClaimsReissue` types the flag, and on `claimsStale` Settings says the old value may show for up to an hour (the access token's lifetime, after which `ensureSession` renews) and skips the account-type reload. The header currency switcher, which never re-minted at all, is covered by the same route. (d) `ensureSession` now reports `unavailable`; the `(dashboard)` guard throws `HttpError(503)` on it instead of bouncing to `/login`, and `_error.tsx` answers a 503 with "Projective is briefly unavailable … You're still signed in" and a **Try again** link to the same URL. The `[handle]`, `(standalone)` and `/explore` renewals still fall back to the guest view during an outage — correct for public pages, and the cookies are kept. **FLAGS for a human:** (a) `documentation/architecture/MVP_FLOW_AUDIT.md`, which the task cited, does not exist (already #189(b)); (e) `429` is classed as transient — a rate-limited refresh keeps the session; (f) the 503 copy assumes the guard is the only `HttpError(503)` thrower, which is true today — a future thrower would need its own copy. | |

| 201 | **Session cookies carry `Secure` on any HTTPS request, and "Keep me signed in" decides the refresh cookie's lifetime (2026-10-13).** MVP flow audit rows 1.2 and 1.6. **(A) THE DEFECTS.** `apps/web/utils/auth-cookies.ts` appended `Secure` only when `DENO_ENV === "production"`, so an HTTPS staging deploy without that variable shipped the `sb-*` session cookies, the PKCE verifier and the pending-verification cookie without it. Separately, `LoginSchema.remember` (the sign-in form's "Keep me signed in") reached `AuthBackendService.authenticate` and was dropped, so every session got a 30-day refresh cookie. Reproduced before the fix: a login over `https://` with `DENO_ENV` unset and `remember: false` answered `sb-refresh-token=…; Max-Age=2592000` with no `Secure`. **(B) SECURE.** Every cookie builder now takes the request it answers (`sessionSetCookies(req, tokens)`, `sessionClearCookies(req)`, `pendingVerificationSetCookie(req, …)`, `oauthStoreCookies(req, …)`, and `toAuthResponse(req, result)` in `features/auth/core/respond.ts`). `isSecureRequest(req)` is true in production, for an `https:` request URL, or when the first hop of `X-Forwarded-Proto` is `https` (a TLS-terminating proxy). Plain `http://localhost` stays insecure, so local development keeps working. **(C) LIFETIME.** `SessionTokens.remember?: boolean` (`ServiceResult.ts`): `authenticate` sets it from the input (default `false`, matching `LoginSchema`). `true` gives the 30-day refresh cookie. `false` gives a refresh cookie with no `Max-Age` (browser-session lifetime) plus an HttpOnly, browser-session `pj_session_transient=1` flag. A renewal (`POST /api/auth/refresh`, `ensureSession`, `renewSession`) leaves `remember` unset and inherits the request's flag, so a transient session stays transient and a remembered one keeps its 30 days. A sign-in with `remember: true` clears a flag still present, and sign-out clears it. A browser with no flag is a remembered session, so sessions minted before this change keep their 30 days. The access cookie keeps its `expires_in` `Max-Age` in both modes, because the `(dashboard)` guard renews when it lapses. **(D) TESTS.** `apps/web/utils/auth-cookies.test.ts` (15): `Secure` by scheme, forwarded proto and production; both lifetimes; inheritance across the refresh route and `ensureSession`; the flag cleared on a remembered sign-in and on logout; the login route forwarding `remember`. `respond.test.ts` updated for the new signature. AMENDS SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE §Sessions & Google OAuth and PRODUCT_SPEC §Authentication surfaces. **FLAGS for a human:** (a) `X-Forwarded-Proto` is trusted from any client, with no trusted-proxy list. A forged `https` can only ADD `Secure`, so the sender only loses its own cookies over plain http. (b) Browsers that restore the previous session ("continue where you left off") also restore session cookies, so `remember: false` is best-effort. (c) After a restart the access cookie can outlive the browser session by up to its `expires_in` (about an hour). With no refresh cookie, the session then ends at the first renewal. (d) Google OAuth, SSO, the confirmation link and `/verify` have no remember choice: they inherit the browser's current flag, normally remembered. (e) An API caller that omits `remember` gets a transient session (the `LoginSchema` default). The form's checkbox defaults to on. (f) `documentation/architecture/MVP_FLOW_AUDIT.md`, which the brief cites, exists only on `origin/claude/adoring-bohr-hdy9qt`, not on `main`. |

| 205 | **The `sb-access-token` cookie is verified, not trusted by presence (2026-10-13). CLOSES the verification TODO of Decisions #14 / #16 / #46; RESOLVES #14's `pj_auth_session` flag.** **(A) THE DEFECT.** The global middleware set `isAuthenticated` from cookie presence and `ensureSession` admitted any present access cookie, so a tampered, foreign or expired token reached `(dashboard)` pages (then failed every RLS read for up to an hour) and was bounced off `/login` to `/home` — reproduced against `HEAD` 14937cd with a payload-rewritten ES256 token: the dashboard rendered, `/login` answered 302 → `/home`. **(B) THE VERIFIER** (`packages/backend/core/access-token.ts`, `createAccessTokenVerifier`). The key is chosen strictly by the token's `alg`, so neither can stand in for the other: `ES256` / `RS256` against the project's public JWKS (`{SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json`, by `kid`); `HS256` against `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` (placeholder = absent); `none` and anything else refused. Then `exp` (required, 30 s leeway) and a user session's claims — `sub` and `aud` `authenticated` — which refuses a hosted project's legacy anon / service-role key, itself an HS256 JWT signed with the same secret. The local CLI stack signs user tokens `ES256` (verified against the running stack: a real token passes, a payload-rewritten one fails on signature). JWKS cached 10 min (single-flight); an unknown `kid` refetches at most once per 30 s, so a rotation is picked up and a spray of made-up kids costs one fetch; a failed refetch keeps serving the keys held; a verifier that never obtained keys answers `unavailable`; each fetch is capped at 3 s. No new dependency (`djwt` + WebCrypto). **(C) THE SEAM.** `AuthBackendService.verifyAccessToken(token)` → `ServiceResult<{ verified }>`: `ok` admits, `401` refuses (`details.reason`), `503` = keys unobtainable — the `refreshSession` convention (#193). Stub mode (auth backend not live, outside `DENO_ENV=production`) answers `ok` with `verified: false`: `dev:mock` and stub sessions are opaque or hand-made tokens with no issuer to check. Production always verifies, whatever the gate says. **(D) THE MIDDLEWARES.** `session.ts` `verifyAccessCookie(req)` runs the check once per request (a `WeakMap` on the `Request`). The global middleware stamps `isAuthenticated` / `userContext` through `resolveRequestViewer`: signed in only on a valid token, otherwise the guest context — so the `(public)/(auth)` guard bounces only a VALID session. `ensureSession`: valid → fast path; invalid or expired + refresh cookie → the existing renewal (refused → clear + `/login?redirectTo=`; outage → `503`, cookies kept); invalid + no refresh cookie → clear both cookies, unauthenticated (the dashboard redirects, `[handle]` / `(standalone)` / `/explore` append the clears and render as a guest); keys unobtainable → `unavailable` (`503` in the dashboard). No loop: the auth-screen guard bounces exactly what the dashboard admits, and `safeRedirect` refuses auth paths. `/api/auth/verification-status` reads the verified `ctx.state.isAuthenticated`; `hasSessionCookie` and `CookieKeys.AUTH_SESSION_TOKEN` (`pj_auth_session`, never set) are deleted. **(E) ENV.** The contract's unread `JWT_SECRET` is renamed `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` (`serverEnv().supabaseJwtSecret`, `.env.example`). No schema change. **(F) TESTS.** `core/access-token.test.ts` (13: ES256 · RS256 · HS256 with and without the secret · rewritten payload · foreign key · `none` / unknown alg / garbage · HS256 signed with the public key · expiry + leeway · anon-key and subject-less tokens · JWKS reuse, rotation, kid-spray throttle, outage, stale keys on a failed refetch) and `utils/session-verify.test.ts` (10, the real guards with a stubbed JWKS `fetch`: valid · tampered without / with a refresh cookie · expired with a refresh cookie (renewed / refused) · expired without · keys unobtainable → 503 · the auth-screen guard on valid vs tampered / expired · a stub-mode opaque session still admitted). **FLAGS for a human:** (a) local verification cannot see revocation — an access token whose session was revoked elsewhere passes until its `exp` (≤ 1 h); its refresh token is dead, and RLS is the backstop in between; closing it needs a per-request GoTrue `getUser` or a session-id check against `auth.sessions`; (b) `deno task dev` with `AUTH_BACKEND_LIVE=true` now refuses forged or opaque cookies — hand-made JWT probes work only under `dev:mock` or with the auth backend off; (c) `/api/*` routes that fall back to `readCookies(req)[SB_ACCESS_COOKIE]` (`api-session.ts`, `user/me.ts`, `user/setup.ts`, `user/preferences.ts`, `view/core/booking-actor.ts`) still hand the raw cookie to services rather than the verified state — PostgREST re-verifies it, so data stays safe, but they do not consult the verifier; (d) `CookieKeys.AUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN` (`pj_auth_refresh`) is equally unused and misnamed — left in place, outside this brief; (e) the brief named `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` "per the env contract", which listed `JWT_SECRET` — renamed rather than duplicated, since nothing read it; (f) the brief's `documentation/architecture/MVP_FLOW_AUDIT.md` exists only on `origin/claude/adoring-bohr-hdy9qt` (5c6dfa97), not on this branch; its row 1.7 "Residual" is what this closes. A refused lock or order sets `settled_unapplied` and the payer's `wallet.topup_succeeded` notification is titled "Payment received — the funds are in your wallet". A completed claim is answered with the payment's `transaction_id`; one whose payment has no ledger row is released and re-processed (the payment row's own status, not the claim, prevents a second credit). Tests: `payments.contract.test.ts` (SQL settled set = SSOT, reason CHECK, release grant), `stripe-webhook.test.ts` (foreign intent ignored; `requireLedgerRow`), `funding-state.test.ts` (`settled_unapplied` → Failed). **(G) VERIFIED.** A private Supabase stack built from `fix/ledger-append-only` + this change applied every migration and seed from scratch; on it `card_settlement_ledger.sql` passed all 13 checks and `ledger_immutability`, `single_ticket_purchase`, `escrow_settlement_authority`, `paid_revisions`, `cohort_session_isolation` and `comms_column_grants` passed. **FLAGS for a human:** (a) **the shared local DB is NOT migrated** — an enum value cannot be added inside a rolled-back dry run and the shared DB is not reset by an agent; nothing breaks meanwhile (the TS reads `unapplied_reason` from `select("*")` with a null fallback), but the new behaviour is live only after `deno task db:reset`. RESOLVES #186 flag (a) and #156 flag (h). **(A) THE DEFECT.** Five `cron.schedule` calls sat in guarded `DO` blocks beside their functions (`archive-stale-service-drafts`, `auto-release-session-escrow`, `finance-billing-cycle`, and on the unmerged M3 / M4 branches `finance-reconcile-wallets`, `finance-mature-pending-releases`); a failed registration left only a `NOTICE` in the migration output. The brief's premise that local `supabase start` lacks pg_cron is stale: the shared DB runs pg_cron 1.6.4 (three jobs, 24 succeeded runs), pg_net 0.20.4 is available, and Vault is installed. **(B) THE HUMAN RULING (2026-10-13):** hosted pg_cron + pg_net calling the routes with the bearer from Vault, not an external runner (no hosting doc says otherwise); deposits hourly and erasures daily, with the cadence configurable; pg_net may be installed in `00000002` under the same guard. **(C) THE REGISTRY.** `ops.scheduled_jobs` (00000013) holds every job: `sql` (one `SELECT`) or `http` (`path` + `secret_name`). An AFTER INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE trigger (00001897) applies the row to pg_cron in the same transaction, so **the cadence is configurable in one place**: the seed (`00005060`) sets the default, and `UPDATE ops.scheduled_jobs SET schedule = … / enabled = false` reschedules or pauses a running database (pg_cron refuses an invalid expression with the write, `22023`). The five DO blocks are gone; their functions now point at the registry. M3 / M4 are seeded only `WHERE to_regprocedure(…) IS NOT NULL`, so the seed holds whichever order those branches merge in. **(D) HTTP DISPATCH.** `ops.fn_dispatch_http_job` reads `CRON_APP_URL` and the row's `secret_name` from `vault.decrypted_secrets` (the secret name is also the app's env key) and queues `net.http_post` (120 s timeout); `ops.http_job_dispatches` records each request, and `ops-watch-jobs` (every 10 min) settles it from `net._http_response` (6 h TTL; unanswered after 7 h is reported). Cadences: `finance-recurring-deposits` hourly at :15 (`limit=50`), `account-erasures` daily 04:10 UTC (`limit=100`). **(E) NOTHING SILENT.** Every skip or failure raises a `WARNING` and writes an `ops.log_entries` row (`scope = 'ops.scheduler'`, `client_id = 'scheduler:<job>:<reason>'`): `pg_cron_unavailable` / `schedule_failed` at registration; `pg_net_unavailable` / `vault_unavailable` / `app_url_missing` / `secret_missing` at dispatch (one row a day per job and reason); `dispatch_failed`, `http_failed`, `no_response`, and `run_failed` (a sql job that raised, read from `cron.job_run_details` once per run). `00000002` can only warn, because the `ops` tables do not exist there yet. **(F) MANUAL RUNS.** `deno task cron:run <job>` / `--list` (`scripts/cron-run.ts` → `ScheduledJobsBackendService`): a sql job through `ops.run_job` (service role only, returns the result as jsonb), an http job POSTed to `APP_URL` + path with the bearer from `.env.local`. Types: `@projective/types/ops`. **(G) VERIFIED** on a private stack reset from `main` + this change (the shared DB was not reset): probe checks 1–7 pass (registration, registry ↔ `cron.job`, reschedule / disable / invalid refused, loud unconfigured skips, the queued request and its bearer, settlement of a 404 and a lost response, grants, failed-run reporting); end to end, pg_net reached a host stub from the container with the Vault bearer (deposits 200, a wrong erasures bearer 404 → one `http_failed` row), pg_cron fired the dispatch itself on a one-minute schedule, and `cron:run` ran `finance-billing-cycle` (14 statements), POSTed deposits (200) and refused a placeholder bearer and an unknown job. **FLAGS for a human:** (a) **implemented sweeps that no migration has ever scheduled**: comms `fn_process_queue`, `fn_escalate_unread`, `fn_build_digests` (daily, weekly), `fn_sweep_expired`, `fn_reap_dead_devices`, `fn_compact_delivery_events` (`database/comms/Functions.md` documented them as registered; now marked not registered), `projects.fn_release_expired_claims` (PRODUCT_SPEC's claim-TTL auto-release depends on it) and `projects.fn_resolve_expired_workload_reports`. (b) The Vault secrets are provisioned nowhere: until `CRON_APP_URL` and the two bearers exist in an environment, each http job skips and logs once a day. | 202 | **The withdrawal lifecycle after the Stripe Transfer (2026-10-13).** MVP audit row 3.8, §2.5 and Phase 0.6 (`documentation/architecture/MVP_FLOW_AUDIT.md`, present only on `origin/claude/adoring-bohr-hdy9qt`). **(A) THE GAPS.** Only `transfer.created` was handled; the seeded `payout.failed` notification had no sender; a transient Stripe error answered 202 and left the payout `pending` and debited with nothing to close it; `destinationId` was accepted by `WithdrawInputSchema`, sent by `WalletDialogs` and dropped in `wallet-actions.ts`; there was no minimum. Reproduced first: `supabase/probes/payout_lifecycle.sql` aborted on the unfixed schema (no minimum), and the planner tests for `transfer.reversed` / `payout.*` did not type-check. **(B) REVERSAL.** `finance.record_transfer_reversed` (processor door) finds the payout by its bound transfer or metadata id, checks the transfer agrees with it, and credits only what is newly reversed (`LEAST(amount_reversed, amount) − reversed_cents`, reason `payout_reversal`), so a replay, a duplicate or an out-of-order lower total credits nothing; a full reversal is the new `payout_status` value `reversed`, a partial one stays `paid`. Person owners get `payout.reversed`. A reversal of, or a `transfer.created` for, a payout already `failed` moves nothing and writes an `ops.log_entries` error (the money left twice). **(C) BANK PAYOUT.** Connect `payout.paid` / `payout.failed` are planned only with `event.account` (a payout without it is the platform's own); the service reads the bank payout's balance transactions on the connected account into the transfers it carried (`payment` → `source_transfer`) and the earlier failed payouts it re-pays (`payout_failure`), and `finance.record_bank_payout` records `bank_status` / `bank_payout_ref` / `bank_failure_code` / `bank_status_at` on the owner's sent payouts. A failure is final for its own bank payout; a later payout that re-pays it marks it paid; nothing moves in the ledger; person owners get `payout.failed` / `payout.paid` (new key). `STRIPE_CONNECT_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (new, optional) signs the Connect destination; the snapshot endpoint verifies against either secret (`verifyStripeEventWithAny`). **(D) STALE SWEEP.** `finance.fn_claim_stale_payouts(p_limit)` leases `pending` payouts older than `payout_stale_minutes` (15) under `SKIP LOCKED` (`swept_at`, `sweep_attempts`); `PaymentBackendService.sweepStalePayouts` finds each transfer by its new group `projective_payout_<id>`, then by scanning the recorded `destination_account`'s transfers for the metadata id, and completes the payout; with none it re-sends under the same idempotency key inside 23 h (Stripe keeps a key 24 h) and calls `fail_payout` after (money back; `fail_payout` now tells person owners `payout.failed`). The decision is the pure `planStalePayout` (`payout-sweep.ts`). `POST /api/finance/cron/payouts` (bearer `FINANCE_CRON_SECRET`, 404 otherwise) is registered as the R2 (#203) job `finance-sweep-stale-payouts`, every 10 minutes, seeded only where the claim function exists. **(E) DESTINATION.** `begin_payout` gains `p_destination_method_id DEFAULT NULL` (one signature): it must be one of the wallet owner's `payout`/`both`, `active` methods by the person-type rule (someone else's reads as missing, `42501`; inactive `PA403`), is recorded on the payout, hashed into the attempt key and stamped on the transfer's metadata. `WithdrawInputSchema.destinationId` is now a uuid. **(F) MINIMUM.** `min_withdrawal_minor` is a per-currency object with a `default` (≈ £10 each, `finance-model.md` §13), read by `finance.fn_min_withdrawal_minor`; `begin_payout` refuses below it (`22023`, "amountMinor: the smallest withdrawal is 10.00 GBP"). **VERIFIED** on a private Supabase stack reset from `14937cd` + this SQL: the probe 32/32 PASS; `function_grants`, `ledger_immutability` and `pending_window` probes clean; `deno task smoke:stripe` all green against stripe-mock and that stack; `deno task check` passes; unit tests pass bar the four pre-existing `theme-engine` failures. **FLAGGED — for a human:** (a) **NEW CONFLICT.** `finance-model.md` §8 "Failed Withdrawal" says the funds "bounce back to their Personal Wallet (Available state)"; with Separate Charges & Transfers a connected account's failed bank payout returns to that account's Stripe balance, not the platform, and the brief asked for a status and a notification. Built as briefed; §8 carries a flag, not a rewrite. Choose: leave the money in the Connect balance (Stripe pays it again once the bank details are fixed), or reverse the transfer on `payout.failed` so (B) credits the wallet. (b) A Transfer cannot target a bank account: the connected account's DEFAULT external account receives Stripe's payout, so `destinationId` is validated, recorded and stamped but does not route money; that needs manual payouts on the connected account. No live path creates payout methods yet (they are seeded only). (c) Only person owners are notified (as `complete_payout` already did); team and business withdrawers are not told of a bank failure or a reversal. | 210 | **Pipeline escrow semantics — the Chain Reaction holds the same ticket's next stage on approval, from the live balance, per-stage switchable; the column lock is a derived board rule (2026-10-13). Product-owner ruling on audit 2.17 / §2.6(e) (`MVP_FIX_PROMPTS.md` P2).** **(A) THE RULINGS.** Asked four questions, the product owner chose: a "column lock" is *no entry into a work column without held escrow* (not a frozen column while in review); "Ticket B" is *the same ticket's next required stage* (not the next backlog ticket); the hold draws on the *live wallet balance*, short → Needs funding + notify (no pre-authorised budget, no wallet reservation — Decision #165 had already declined a reservation concept); and the chain is a *per-stage toggle, default on*. PRODUCT_SPEC's "Approval of Ticket A … locks Escrow for Ticket B" is re-worded to say so. **(B) WHAT ALREADY EXISTED.** Every approval — an accepted submission and `approve_stage` — already settles through `fn_settle_ticket_stage` → `projects.force_complete_stage`, which released the stage, advanced the ticket and re-held (`PF402` → `todo` / Needs funding). The audit missed it because nothing named it a chain. **(C) THE TOGGLE.** `projects.project_stages.chain_reaction boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true`, read on the RECEIVING stage (the hold is that stage's money and its lock trigger). Off, `force_complete_stage` moves the ticket there `todo` with `payment_status = 'unpaid'` (Draft) — NOT `partially_released`, because every "fundable" gate (`fund_ticket`, `fund_stage`, `fn_stage_funding_need`) accepts only `unpaid` / `needs_funding`, and the payment axis describes the CURRENT stage, exactly as `fn_mark_needs_funding` already overwrites it on a refusal. Edited in the stage's Advanced settings ("Fund on arrival", `SetupStageFields`, not offered on the first stage, a session or a personal project) through the existing setup PATCH (owner RLS on `project_stages`, no new RPC); read-only in the StageInspector. `StageSetupSchema.chainReaction` has NO Zod default on purpose: `UpdateProjectSchema` is it `.partial()`, and Zod 4 applies a default through `.partial()`, so a save that omitted the field would have switched it back on. **(D) OUTCOMES + NOTICES.** One `ticket_history` row per outcome (`chain_held` · `chain_needs_funding` · `chain_off`, read by the board as `funding` entries naming the stage); the refused path tags `fn_mark_needs_funding`'s DETAIL `trigger: chain_reaction`; a wait (refused or off) tells the assignee a new catalog key `ticket.awaiting_funding` (work · high · in_app/push/email); a hold already tells them "Funded — you can start". **(E) THE COLUMN LOCK IS DERIVED, NOT STORED.** No `board_columns` table exists (the audit's `projects.board_columns.locked_by_escrow` was invented) and board columns map 1:1 to `ticket_status`, so the lock is `workColumnLocked(card, toStatus)` in `@projective/types/projects`: a CLAIMED ticket, entering `claimed`/`in_progress`/`in_review` from outside work, not personal, whose `funding.canStart` is false — the #165 gate on `trg_ticket_escrow_sync` shown before the drop. An unclaimed ticket is never locked: its drop is the claim, which is the lock trigger. `@projective/ui/kanban` gains `itemDropRefusal(item, column) → reason | null` (locked column styling, reason line, announcement); the board island also re-checks in `onItemMove`. **(F) DEV CONTEXT SWITCHER — NO NEW AXIS.** The lock is derived from the funding state, so the existing **Funding state** axis now drives it too (the island reads it through `previewFunding`); the toggle is real stage data edited in the UI, not a simulated axis. **VERIFIED** — `supabase/probes/chain_reaction.sql`, 23 checks rolled back (held / refused / off / gate / `fund_ticket` / `approve_stage`), plus `approval_settlement`, `escrow_settlement_authority`, `fair_exit_settlement`, `stage_funding_prepaid` unchanged (108 checks); APPLIED by the user-approved 2026-10-13 reset and re-probed live (23/23). `column-lock.test.ts` (7) and `live-board.test.ts` (chain history, stage flag). **FLAGGED — for a human:** (a) the chained hold keeps the ticket's CURRENT assignee as payee in the next stage unless a team holds that stage — a different freelancer staffing stage 2 is not re-routed (pre-existing in `force_complete_stage`); (b) `live-board.ts` `escrowHeldOf` reads `partially_released` as held — harmless to the lock (it reads `funding.canStart`) but wrong on the card's `escrowHeld` flag. |
| 211 | **Session settlement beyond cohort seats — 1-1 sessions and set-session blocks are payable, hold ONE ESCROW PER SITTING, release per sitting by negative consent, cancel per sitting, and a block's n-1 sittings are agreed through 72-hour scheduling handshakes (2026-10-13). Product-owner rulings, the same day: wire 1-1 payment here; one escrow per sitting; provisional weekly sittings + a 72h handshake whose lapse keeps the pencilled-in time.** MVP audit rows 2.18 / 2.19, work order X2. **(A) THE DEFECTS.** `finance.auto_release_session_escrow` released only cohort SEAT escrows; the provider-cancel → auto-refund and the late-cancel forfeit existed only for seats; a set-session block booked one slot and nothing scheduled the other n-1. The first slot is re-tested against the provider's schedule under a row lock (conflict + blackout), so two buyers paying for one slot cannot both be seated — the second is refused PS409 and charged nothing. The checkout's `walletSettles` accepts a session line that carries its time. **(C) NEGATIVE CONSENT, GENERALISED.** The sweep releases every session escrow with no open dispute (`finance.fn_escrow_has_open_dispute`, the dispute work order's predicate) `session_payout_hours` after its sitting ended: a 1-1 sitting's escrow after ITS sitting, a cohort seat's after the cohort's last (unchanged). A provider no-show refunds the escrow its sitting stands for, at ANY age — the 24h window on that path is dropped, since the escrow still being `held` is the only guard needed and a missed sweep must not forfeit a refund. A per-sitting move ends the seat only when nothing is left held (`projects.fn_settle_membership_state`: `completed` if any sitting paid the provider, else `cancelled`); a sitting that happened still pays out on a cancelled booking. **(D) CANCELLATION.** PRODUCT_SPEC §Session-Based C already rules the money (>24h refund · <24h forfeit to the freelancer · freelancer cancel = full refund any time; no partial fee — the 50% figure was retired earlier), so nothing was asked: `cancel_cohort_membership` applies it PER SITTING against each sitting's own start on a 1-1 — a client cancelling a block across the notice line comes out `partial` (far sittings refunded, near ones forfeited) — and leaves a sitting that has already started to settle on its own window or dispute. Each cancelled sitting is marked `cancelled_by_freelancer` / `cancelled_by_client`, leaves the calendar, has its open handshake withdrawn, and the one-seat cohort ends. The other party is notified (`session.cancelled`, with refunded / forfeited minor units). **(E) THE N-1 HANDSHAKES.** Each provisional sitting gets a 1-on-1 reschedule round (round 0, `counterparty`, `collecting` — the provider proposes, the client accepts or counters, the Proactive Calendar's existing flow) due `set_session_schedule_hours` (72, new param) after payment and never later than `session_cancel_notice_hours` before the provisional start. `projects.fn_lapse_session_handshakes` (job `session-scheduling-handshakes`, every 15 min) lapses each round still open at its deadline through `scheduling.close_reschedule_round` — `lapsed` already means "the original time stands" — and tells both people (`session.scheduling_lapsed`). Both are told at payment (`session.scheduling_requested`); the same sweep reminds the provider ONCE, 24h before the booking's earliest open deadline (`session.scheduling_reminder` — the notification row is the "sent" mark). The reminder is deliberately NOT routed through `comms.notification_queue`: its worker `comms.fn_process_queue` is unscheduled pending Decision #203 flag (a), and registering it would start every queued reminder platform-wide — that ruling stays with a human. Two triggers (00001860): `trg_sitting_follows_calendar` moves a sitting with its calendar mirror (which also fixes the adjacent defect for group sittings), and `trg_session_handshake_closed` confirms a provisional sitting when its round rests. **(F) DEV CONTEXT SWITCHER — NO NEW AXIS.** Nothing here is a simulated persona, capability or flag: per-sitting funding and handshakes are real data. **VERIFIED** — `supabase/probes/session_settlement.sql` in one rolled-back transaction over the on-disk `00001155` / `00001210` / `00001860` (end to end through `place_wallet_order` as the buyer: payment, slot clash, stale price, past time, handshake carried and lapsed, per-sitting release / dispute hold / 100h no-show refund, partial client cancel, provider cancel inside the window, cohort-seat regression, grants, job registry — 17 checks), and on the same in-flight definitions `cohort_session_isolation`, `single_ticket_purchase`, `scheduled_jobs`, `function_grants`, `paid_revisions` unchanged; `catalog.contract.test.ts`, `payments.contract.test.ts`. **NOT APPLIED** to the shared local DB (needs a user-approved reset or definitions apply). **FLAGGED — for a human:** (a) no UI calls the cancel door (`SessionService.cancelSeat`) — the provider-cancel → refund path is reachable by API only; (c) the 12h reschedule lockout vs the 24h cancel window (`PRODUCT_MANAGEMENT.md`'s standing flag) now also applies to block sittings; (d) the session engagement gets no Discussion room — `comms.get_or_create_project_channel` authorises the caller, who at payment is the buyer; The provider-no-show auto-refund also looked only at sittings that ended inside the payout window, so a missed sweep never refunded (dropped by #211 at our request). **(B) THE LIFECYCLE (PRODUCT_MANAGEMENT §3.8, `dispute_status` edited in place).** `open` — raised; the room's logs are complete only when the sitting ends. At the end the attendance audit (`finance.fn_dispute_attendance_audit`) is PRODUCT_SPEC §Dispute Resolution 3's deterministic ruling: `fn_session_presence` = `provider_no_show` → **instant refund**; a tracked room with the host AND the claimant each in it ≥ `dispute_dismiss_presence_pct` (80) % of the sitting → **dismissed** (webhook rows only — a host attestation cannot dismiss a claim against the host); anything else, an untracked room included → `awaiting_response` with `respond_by` = now + `dispute_response_hours` (48, the spec's cooling-off) and `dispute.response_requested` to the provider. The respondent's statement, either party's escalation, or the deadline (the sweep — the auto-escalation) → `under_review`. An operator (`security.is_admin()`, `ops.admin_users`) rules release · refund · split with reasons. The old `resolved` / `refunded` had no writer and are gone. **(C) SCHEMA (00000017).** `finance.disputes` gains `session_event_id`, `audit`, `respond_by`, `responded_at`, `escalated_at`, `resolved_by`, `payee_share_bp`, `settlement`, `updated_at` and three CHECKs; `escrow_id` CASCADE → RESTRICT (a dispute outlives anything it is about). `finance.dispute_messages` gains `party`; new `finance.dispute_evidence` (statement ↔ `files.items`, RESTRICT). RLS: `dispute_evidence` readable through its dispute; no client writes to any dispute table. **(D) FUNCTIONS (new 00001260).** `fn_escrow_has_open_dispute` (THE live predicate — #211's release paths, the claim and the workspace call it), `fn_settle_dispute` (the one writer of a resolved status; release → `fn_release_seat_escrow`, refund → `fn_refund_seat_escrow`, split → new `fn_split_seat_escrow` on `fn_fair_exit_split`'s arithmetic; the seat follows through #211's `fn_settle_membership_state`; an escrow already settled elsewhere is recorded `by_fact`; a chargeback-frozen one waits), `fn_advance_dispute`, `respond_to_dispute` (statement + ≤ 10 own uploaded files), `escalate_dispute`, `get_dispute`, `resolve_dispute` (operator), `sweep_disputes` (`finance-dispute-sweep`, :07/:22/:37/:52). `claim_session_no_show` now names the sitting, picks the escrow that pays for THIS sitting (per-sitting first, #211), notifies `dispute.opened` instead of the chargeback's `escrow.disputed`, and audits at once after the end; `get_session_workspace` adds `disputes` and `claimable_sitting_id`. New catalog keys `dispute.response_requested`, `dispute.escalated`. **(E) SERVICE, ROUTES, UI.** `DisputeBackendService` (`packages/backend/services/finance/` — PRODUCT_SPEC's `DisputeService`, named by the folder's `*BackendService` convention) + `dispute-model.ts`; `GET /api/finance/disputes/:id`, `POST …/respond`, `…/escalate`, `…/resolve`; the no-show route gains Zod (`NoShowClaimInputSchema`). | 213 | **Approval never settles a ticket it has nobody to pay — a stage nobody was hired on is refused, an unclaimed prepaid ticket on a hired stage is refunded and left open, and the counts say which; plus the post-wave-7 small gaps: a confirm before Accept & release payment, one live flag for listing + instantiation, pre-settlement assignee notices, the wallet Standing's effective fee, and the two probes that predate the pending window (2026-10-13).** Post-wave-7 gap closure (`MVP_FLOW_AUDIT.md` / `MVP_FIX_PROMPTS.md`), CLOSES #197 flag (d), #194 flags (a) and (e), #191 flag (e). **(A) THE DEFECT** (reproduced on the shared DB in a rolled-back run before any edit): funding an OPEN stage through `fund_stage` holds one prepaid escrow per ticket with no payee (#197); `approve_stage` then pushed every such ticket through `fn_settle_ticket_stage` → `force_complete_stage`, so both tickets landed `completed` while `fn_release_ticket_escrow` refunded their escrows (`payment_status` back to `unpaid` on a completed ticket), the stage went `paid`, and the result said `released_count` 2 with `total_paid_cents` 0 — work recorded as done and paid that nobody was hired to do. **(B) THE RULE (00001150 §6, edited in place).** Approval pays whoever was hired. With no BOUND escrow on the stage — held or already released (an acceptance) — `approve_stage` refuses before anything moves (`55000`, "Nobody has been hired on this stage — its prepaid escrow waits for a freelancer to claim a ticket, so there is no one to pay yet."; the old "No funded (held) escrow" refusal stays for a stage nothing was funded on). The payment stays `processing`, uncredited, and `finance.v_ops_unledgered_payments` lists it as `problem = 'settlement_mismatch'` (new trailing columns `stripe_event_id`, `reported_amount_cents`, `reported_currency`) until a human settles or closes it. #200's rule stands for everything transient: no payment bound yet still releases the claim, a settlement that raised still rolls its claim back, both 5xx. **(B) DEPOSITS.** `claim_due_deposit_rules` advanced `next_run_at` at claim time; a transient Stripe/network error left the run `requires_payment` with no PaymentIntent and nothing picked it up again, so the period was lost. Lease: `updated_at` older than 15 minutes, re-stamped, `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (index `idx_inbound_payments_unbound_deposits`). A run older than 23 hours is never re-sent (Stripe keeps a key 24 hours) — `failed` with an ops error row (`reason = 'unbound_expired'`), no strike; a run whose rule stopped or whose author, card or Customer no longer passes is `canceled` with a warn row (`unbound_canceled`). The re-authorisation moved into internal `finance.fn_deposit_charge_target` (revoked from every role). Only a declined card or required authentication counts a strike; transient, misconfigured and `StripeIdempotencyError` (key still in flight) leave the run for the next sweep; a bind that fails after Stripe created the intent leaves it pending and the next sweep binds the same intent; the sweep never throws (a refusal's failed bind used to abort it). | 218 | **Listing analytics are written and the client pipeline is one read — `analytics.fn_rollup_listings` (daily job `analytics-listing-rollups`), `fn_subject_visible('listing')`, and `catalogue.get_client_pipeline` with a narrow definer for the buyer's order lines (2026-10-14).** Work order C5 of #217. BUILDS ON #203 (job registry), #217 flags (g) / (k). **(A) ROLLUPS.** `analytics.daily_rollups` had no writer, so every catalogue figure was fabricated (`API_BACKLOG.md` P1 #33 gap (a), P2 #1). `analytics.fn_rollup_listings(p_day)` (definer, service role only) writes one UTC day as `subject_kind = 'listing'` rows: `listing.impressions` · `clicks` · `views` (distinct sessions) · `checkout_starts` · `orders` · `gross_minor {currency}` · `bookings` · `booking_slot {dow, hour}` in the seller's timezone (owning schedule → profile → UTC) · `query_impressions {q}` and `query_clicks {q}` (5+ distinct sessions only; `query_clicks` is ADDED beyond the brief because `KeywordRow.clicks` (C1) needs it) · `cancellations` (refunded / cancelled non-session lines by the order's last change, plus sittings cancelled). It upserts on the rollup key AND deletes the day's listing rows it no longer produces, so a re-run equals one fresh computation; `fn_backfill_listing_rollups(p_from, p_to)` loops days (≤ 2 years). Registered through the #203 seed (`00005060`), `SELECT analytics.fn_rollup_listings(current_date - 1)` daily 02:10 UTC; `scheduled_jobs.sql` expects it. Zod `ListingRollupMetric` + `LISTING_ROLLUP_DIMENSIONS`, pinned to the SQL (names, dimensions, the threshold = `KEYWORD_MIN_SESSIONS`) by `listing-rollups.contract.test.ts`. **(B) VISIBILITY.** `fn_subject_visible` treated `listing` as admin-only; it now answers through new `catalogue.fn_manages_listing`: the owner of a personal listing, or a holder of `publish_listings` on the owning team (a plain member does not see a team listing's analytics — narrower than `get_listing_sales`, which admits any active member). **(C) PIPELINE.** `catalogue.get_client_pipeline(p_listing, p_limit)` is INVOKER over six arms (inquiry thread with `subject_listing_id`, quote request, discovery call, order line, session seat, pipeline project), returning each source table's OWN status (lanes stay in `laneOf`), `action_reasons` (`inquiry_unanswered`, `reschedule_open`, `handshake_pending`, `dispute_open`, `revision_requested`, `submission_pending` = a drafted, unsent submission) and `href`. **RULED by the human (2026-10-14):** the buyer's `finance.orders` / `order_lines` are invisible to a seller under RLS, so the order arm reads through a NARROW definer, `catalogue.fn_seller_order_lines` (buyer, order status and instants, line total, currency — never payment method, card, promo, totals or other sellers' lines), rather than new seller policies on the buyer's whole order row. `catalogue.fn_candidate_listings` (definer) finds the caller's listings by index. `ClientEngagementRowSchema` mirrors the columns (contract test); `ClientEngagement` gains `nextEventAt` and renames `updatedAt` → `lastActivityAt`. **(D) INDEXES.** Every arm checked with `EXPLAIN` under `enable_seqscan = off` on seeded data; seven sequential scans closed: listings by owner / owning team and quote requests by blueprint (new `00004012_indexes_catalogue_marketplace.sql` — neither domain had an index file), order lines by item and three day-range indexes for the rollup (`00004005`), open reschedule rounds and a sitting's calendar mirror (`00004007`), open revision requests (`00004003`). **VERIFIED** on a private stack (`main` + C3's `00000016` / `00000018` / `00000033` + this change): `supabase/probes/listing_analytics.sql` 34/34 (every metric, both day edges, idempotency, stale-row removal, k at 4 → 5, backfill, grants, the job, owner / stranger / team manager / plain member reads, one row per arm for the seller and none for the buyer or a stranger); `function_grants` and `scheduled_jobs` probes pass. **FLAGGED — for a human:** (a) **`href` is not slug-only.** DM threads and calendar events have no slugs, so the inquiry arm links `/messages/<thread uuid>` (ROUTING's own conversation address), quotes and orders `/messages/dm-<handle>`, and calls / sittings `/calendar?event=<event uuid>` — and the calendar does not yet open an event from `?event=` (its modal stack is not URL-synced); C16 must wire it or change the link. (b) **No app path writes `view` events yet**: C3 added `'view'` to the CHECK and the rollup counts distinct sessions, but neither `/view` nor the discovery beacon (`interest-rows.ts`) emits one; no C-prompt names the writer. (c) The plan's seed row ("90 days of synthetic interest events, then the backfill") is not in C5's work order and was not done; seeded analytics stay empty until it is. (d) An order placed by a team, business or enterprise has no `buyer_user_id` (orders record no placing user). (e) A seller sees a buyer's instantiated pipeline project only once engaged on it (`has_project_access`); a draft nobody has invited them to is invisible, by RLS. (f) The shared local DB has none of this DDL until `deno task db:reset`. No interest event is recorded. **(B) CHROME.** `ShellChrome` gains `"bare"` (§D.6): no top bar, rail, lane, bands, `BottomNav` or skip link. The dashboard layout resolves no slots for it and mounts none of its floating hosts. **(C) FRAMING.** A third CSP profile, `framed`: the platform policy with `frame-ancestors 'self'`, sent on every simulate answer. The middleware sends `x-frame-options: SAMEORIGIN` only when a response's policy is EXACTLY that header, and `DENY` otherwise (`frameOptionsFor`). Inside the frame, `PreviewFrameBridge` opens any link that leaves the page in a new tab, and hands the scroll position across reloads (`pj:preview-scroll`: report · ready · restore). **(D) THE GATE.** `features/view/core/simulation.ts` (`commitOrSimulate`, `simulatedOutcomeFor`) and `booking-commits.ts` route every buyer write through one function: pipeline draft, archive, session or seat, scoped brief, quote, question, discovery call, basket, instant checkout, plus the lane menu's save · collection · share. In a simulation the live call is never made; the outcome ("A buyer would now pay £120.00 into escrow at checkout.") is announced and shown beside the control (`data-simulation-outcome`). `booking-commits.test.ts` stubs `fetch`, presses every commit and asserts no request to `/api/(basket\|checkout\|booking\|services)`; with the simulation off the same commits reach their endpoints. The owner's own basket is never read. **(E) PREVIEW TAB.** `PreviewCanvas`: device `SelectButton` → `?device=`, a 1280px desktop frame scaled by `--cat-preview-scale` (pure `previewScale`, written from a ResizeObserver), a 390 × 844 phone in a token-drawn bezel, reload 1.5 s after `saving → saved`, and "Open in a new tab". **VERIFIED** in the browser as `marisdelacroix` on a DRAFT session listing: own listing 200 + SAMEORIGIN, a stranger's 404, the rest of the app still DENY; the framed Book session modal drew 6 slots and committed with zero basket/checkout/booking/services requests; scroll 480 → 480 across a reload; Mobile laid out at 390 × 844 with the buy bar in place of the lane. **FLAGGED — for a human:** (a) **Commit label.** The C14 prompt says a commit "keeps its label and tier"; ruling (j) says it "reads 'Simulated: nothing is booked or charged'". The ruling was followed for every MODAL commit (Book, Request call, Continue, Send request, the question's Send). The page-level CTAs keep their real label and tier — including the three that commit directly (Add to projects, Add to basket, Buy now) — so the page is what a buyer sees; they resolve locally and show the outcome. (b) **Buy now opens no panel in a simulation.** Opening `BuyNowModal` IS a write (it adds the basket line and opens a checkout session on mount), so "every CTA opens its real modal" cannot hold for instant checkout. It resolves on press instead. (c) **Recommendation rails are left out** of the simulation (their cards navigate away from the listing); reviews stay. (d) **Security.** `framed` + `SAMEORIGIN` loosens the "non-negotiable" `x-frame-options` floor for one route; ruling (j) requires it. (e) The scheduler stage's in-calendar booking (`ScheduleView` `onBook`) was already session-local with no network call, and still paints "You're booked" in a simulation. (f) A restricted (13–17) owner's simulation shows the adult buyer's page, not the `RestrictedLaneNotice`. (g) The dev-only Dev Tools launcher renders inside the frame (C17 owns devtools). (h) In the hidden built-in browser pane, a frame present at first paint did not start loading until its `src` was set again; not seen in a visible window. (f) **Dev Context Switcher**: no new axis — `deletable` is derived from live data and the catalogue reads have no fixture branch; say if a `catalogueDeletable` override is wanted. (g) The brief asked for "chips" in the band; gate 7 (anti-tagification) keeps them inline text and unboxed figures. (h) This puts search back in the body toolbar, which #217's rebuild had deliberately moved into the band. (i) `fx-toolbar.css` is imported across features (projects → catalogue); a `packages/ui` home would be cleaner. (j) DONE by #222/#224: the card kebab is `ActionMenu` over the shared `core/listing-menu.ts` (also the table rows), still routed through `requestAction`, so both removals confirm. Scroll is preserved by the bodies, which stay mounted. **(F) VERIFIED.** `deno task check` 0 errors; lint and fmt clean on the changed files; `deno task test:unit` 3,922 passed, only the four `theme-engine.test.ts` failures (#96(a)). A clause that reads the same in two versions is one constant. Every clause constant carries a JSDoc citation (the PRODUCT_SPEC section, the `finance-model.md` section, the decision, or the code that sets a cookie), pinned by `content.test.ts`. URL normalisation (`core/view.ts`): an unknown version is a 404; an empty parameter (what the no-JavaScript form submits) is a 303 to the clean address; `compare` equal to the shown version is dropped and a newer one is swapped; `?v=<current>` is kept, so a pinned link keeps pinning after a newer version takes effect. The view shows each changed clause in full — `<ins>` / `<del>` with visually hidden "Added:" / "Removed:" (a small gap before an insertion only where it starts a new word, `DiffSpan.gap`), a table drawn as the document's own `ui-prose__table` — caption, `<th scope="col">` header row, `<th scope="row">` row headers — and diffed cell by cell (a row whose cell count changed is a removal plus an addition), a unit that did not change word by word (unchanged, added, removed) in its authored inline form so its links and code survive, a "Changed in version X" line that describes the clause's diff group (`aria-describedby`), a 2px gutter bar — folds every run of unchanged clauses behind a native `<details>` ("Show n unchanged clauses"), and the rail lists only the clauses that changed (a removed clause, which has no number in the version shown, takes a dash in the number column). Each version's "What changed in version X" notice under the header links "Compare with version Y" (the version it replaced), so Compare is reachable from the top below the frame's meta-rail width; the oldest version of a multi-version family says what it is ("About version 1.0: …"). **(E) The page.** The document composes P0's primitives — DocumentLayout with `ui-doc--clauses`, DocumentHeader, the TableOfContents island as `<nav aria-label="Legal documents">` listing every document with this one expanded, ReadingProgress, DocumentBody with the "Plain-English summary" label — plus the `LegalVersionControls` island in the meta rail: a `<form method="get">` of native radios (`RadioGroup`) that works without JavaScript, Download PDF, and Print (offered once hydrated; it opens every folded clause run for the print).
