| 276 | **`/contact` is a real intake — one definer door into `ops.contact_requests` on the unified machine, attachments through the files upload pipeline into a private `contact` bucket for signed-in senders only, the dispute intent handed to the dispute flow that exists, and a form that works without JavaScript (2026-10-18). PUBLIC_ROUTES P3; APPLIES #88, #147, #157, #212 and gate 11; EXTENDS `SelectButton` and `RadioGroup` (§C.1); FLAGS (a)–(l) for a human.** **(A) THE RECORD.** `ops.contact_requests` (`00000013`, region `[contact]`): `reference` (`CT-XXXX-XXXX` over Crockford base32 — no I, L, O or U — UNIQUE, minted by `ops.fn_contact_reference()` and re-drawn on a collision; a correlation key the sender quotes, never a route, so #88 is untouched), `intent` (`sales` · `support` · `dispute` · `security`), `status`, `email` (lower-cased; NULL only on an anonymous report), `user_id` (`auth.uid()` at write time; FK `auth.users(id)` — the identity, not the profile, because `/contact` is public and an account that has not finished `/join` has no `org.users_public` row yet but is still a signed-in sender, the one most likely to need support; `ON DELETE SET NULL` so a request outlives its account), `anonymous`, `payload` jsonb (the intent's own fields, ≤ 16 KB, a 20–5,000-character message) — plus `ops.contact_request_attachments` (`request_id`, `file_id` UNIQUE, both `RESTRICT`). The status is the unified machine's own states, stored as is (`backlog → in_progress → complete`, `archived` from any and terminal; PRODUCT_MANAGEMENT §3.5 "Contact request"), and a request is a record: `ops.fn_guard_contact_request` (BEFORE UPDATE, every role) refuses any change but `status` along those moves (and `user_id → NULL`, the erasure FK). Nothing deletes one. **(B) ONE WRITER.** `ops.submit_contact_request(intent, email, anonymous, payload, attachment_ids)` (`00001655`), SECURITY DEFINER, EXECUTE to `anon` and `authenticated` (and `service_role`) — the tables have SELECT for operators (`security.is_admin()`) and no write policy or write grant for any client role. It re-checks everything a direct PostgREST call could forge: the intent; a payload holding only its intent's keys (`CONTACT_PAYLOAD_KEYS`); the message and name lengths; every key's VALUE as the Zod SSOT parses it — `company` 1–160 and `referenceId` 1–200 characters, `accountEmail` an address, `companySize` · `budget` · `topic` · `reportType` from closed lists declared in the function and mirrored value for value from `CONTACT_COMPANY_SIZES` · `CONTACT_BUDGETS` · `CONTACT_SUPPORT_TOPICS` · `CONTACT_SECURITY_REPORTS` (`contact.contract.test.ts` reads them), the engagement exactly `{slug, title, format}` — and the keys every request of the intent stores; an anonymous report is security-only with no address, name, account or file; anything else has a valid reply address. Durable ceilings per rolling hour → `PR429` (5 per address, 10 per account, 60 named requests from guests platform-wide — `anon` reaches the door directly, so rotating addresses would otherwise write, and notify every operator, without bound — and 30 anonymous reports platform-wide, `CONTACT_DB_CEILINGS`) back the service's per-process limiter (10 per IP and 3 per address per ten minutes). A filled honeypot (`ctc_hp`, `autocomplete="off"`, a name no autofill or identity-fill tool targets — a `website` field is one they fill — off-screen and out of the tab order, not `display: none`) is answered with a receipt exactly like a real one and nothing is stored, and the hit is logged through the logging service (the intent, never the body) so a person caught by it is visible; there is no CAPTCHA dependency. An anonymous report is always written as `anon`, signed in or not, so the reporter's token never reaches PostgREST or Postgres (and a lapsed token cannot refuse it); the JSON road reads only a body declared `application/json` (415 otherwise), which another site cannot send without a preflight. Operators are told through `comms.fn_notify('contact.received')` (`00005010` region `[contact]`; in-app + email, digestible, no action URL), which names the intent and the reference, never the sender's words. **(C) MASKING.** Messages are stored as written, not through `comms.mask_pii`: the only readers are operators, and #147 masks copies shown to non-operators — there are none. A future surface that shows a request to anyone else masks its copy first (JSDoc on `ContactBackendService` and the table). **(D) ATTACHMENTS — signed-in senders only.** They reuse the files pipeline's three steps (`/api/contact/attachments/init` → the browser's PUT to a signed URL with byte progress → `/complete`), with one destination change: the declared row is an ordinary `pending_upload` row in the caller's `quarantine` (so `files.fn_guard_pipeline_columns` and the items policies hold unchanged) marked `target_bucket = 'contact'`; the complete step claims it (`scanning`), sniffs the bytes (`classifyContactBytes`: a program or a web page is refused and parked `quarantined`; an unknown or unaccepted type is refused as `error`; neither is kept) and promotes the original into the new private bucket `contact` (10 MiB, PNG · JPEG · WebP · GIF · PDF · plain text, at most 5 a request; `00005040`) as `files.items.purpose = 'contact'` — a new `files.asset_purpose` value, so the uploader's library never lists it. The bucket's one storage policy is operator SELECT of SENT attachments, and `files.fn_can_read` gains an operator arm for a `purpose = 'contact'` row that `ops.contact_request_attachments` links — a file its sender removed (perhaps the wrong, sensitive document) or left on an unsent form is nobody's to read. Unsent files do not linger: Remove works at every step but the brief check (it cancels a running PUT) and takes the file back through `ops.discard_contact_attachment` (the caller's own unlinked row soft-deleted, its bytes deleted by the service); the hourly http job `contact-attachment-sweep` (`POST /api/contact/cron/attachments`, `CONTACT_CRON_SECRET`, `00005060` region `[contact]`) does the same for every contact upload older than six hours that no request links (`ops.fn_claim_stale_contact_attachments`, `SKIP LOCKED`), because storage objects cannot be deleted from SQL. The intake locks the caller's rows before it links them, so a Remove or the sweep and a submission never both win. The library's own complete steps (`/api/files/upload-complete`, `/api/media/upload-complete`) refuse a row with a `target_bucket`, so only the contact pipeline finishes a contact declaration. A guest cannot attach: a `files.items` row and the quarantine policies are anchored on an account, and an anonymous upload path would need its own storage namespace and abuse controls — a guest is told why and may describe the files; an anonymous report carries none, because a file is in its uploader's name. The dropzone prints the bucket's limits before a byte moves and re-checks each file against them; its rows show Uploading (a determinate bar) → Checking the file (`scanning`) → Ready / Not attached with the reason. **(E) THE DISPUTE INTENT.** The only door that OPENS a dispute is a session's Report no-show (`/api/sessions/sittings/:eventId/no-show`, #212); `/api/finance/disputes` is the operator queue. So a signed-in reader picks one of their open engagements (active or on hold, never a personal project; read through the projects feed): a session goes to its project page, where the no-show claim and its escrow hold live; any other engagement is filed to the disputes team with the engagement re-resolved server-side against the caller's OWN engagements (a slug they are not on is refused) and stored as `{slug, title, format}`. A guest gets the sign-in link (`/login?redirectTo=/contact?intent=dispute`) and a reference-ID + message fallback. **(F) WITHOUT JAVASCRIPT.** The intake is a plain `POST /api/contact` form; the route answers with a 303 back to `/contact` — `?sent=1` with the receipt in a ten-minute HttpOnly `Path=/contact` cookie (never in the address bar, history or a Referer) that the page clears once shown, or `?error=` with the fields to mark. A cross-site form post is refused outright. The intent switcher is `SelectButton` with the new `hrefFor`: server-rendered it is a row of links (`aria-current` on the selected one), hydrated the same radiogroup, switching in place with `history.replaceState`. An anonymous report must not need a script (a whistleblower may browse with JavaScript off), so the anonymous control is a real `Checkbox`, not a `ToggleSwitch` (whose `role="switch"` button cannot turn without one): unscripted, CSS hides the name and email while it is ticked, those two inputs carry no `required`, and the form road drops them from an anonymous report before the schema reads it (`submissionFromForm`). On the split canvas (60rem of page — about a `--bp-lg` viewport inside the guest shell's gutters) the four fieldsets share one grid cell, so switching never moves the page; stacked below it, that reserve left a blank band under a shorter form's Send button with the rail and the foot right under it, so there the inactive sets leave the flow (absolute, clipped) and the column takes the active form's height — the narrow-width trade-off of "no height jump", a resize the reader's own switch causes, not layout shift. They cross-fade on `--dur-fast` (opacity only; a cut under both reduced-motion channels); the inactive three are `disabled`, `inert` and `aria-hidden`. The message carries `minlength` (`Textarea` forwards it), so the browser refuses a too-short message before the plain post while what was typed is still on the page; a refusal the server still makes (a rate limit, sign-in, the intake unavailable) returns to the form with only the pre-fill — carrying the fields back was declined, since a 5,000-character message does not fit a cookie. A signed-in reader's name and address open pre-filled from their own session's claims (`contactPrefillFromClaims`, as `/join` re-builds its pre-fill) and stay editable; nothing about who sent a request is taken from them — the writer stamps `auth.uid()`. **(G) THE GATE.** `CONTACT_BACKEND_LIVE` (default off): off, development validates, rate-limits and answers a receipt with nothing stored (attachments checked against their declaration, remembered in-process); production answers 503 rather than acknowledge a request nobody will read. **(H) COMPONENTS.** `SelectButton` gains the described layout (an option's `description` as a meta line on a wrapping grid, the host setting `--sb-described-columns`) and `hrefFor` (links before hydration); `RadioGroup` draws `Option.description` as each radio's accessible description (named by its label alone) and takes `aria-labelledby` for the group; `FormControl`'s render child receives `labelId`; `FileUpload` forwards `aria-describedby` to its zone (the contact zone is described by its limits line); `Textarea` forwards `minLength`. **(I) BUTTONS.** Each form's submit is the column's one filled primary; the work order's "tonal" Book a call is `severity="neutral" variant="outlined"` — the Button Interaction Matrix has no tonal tier and a utility action is tier 4 (#157). **(J) WHAT IS NOT SHOWN.** No platform status line (no health endpoint exists to read one from; a status read from nothing is a fabricated one); no office picture (no address is published to picture); no telephone or email in the `Organization`'s `contactPoint`s (each is its intent's URL). **FLAGS.** **(a) Focus ring — conflict with the owner directive.** The work order asks for "a focus ring per the tokens"; rings are OFF app-wide by product-owner directive (`apps/web/styles/global.css` neutralises `--focus-ring-*`). Shipped: the fields contract's own focus glow, nothing re-added; `global.css` untouched. **(b) No Projective sales profile exists in the seed**, so "Book a discovery call" renders disabled (`aria-disabled`, its reason as visible text and `aria-describedby`, gate 11). Designating one (`PROJECTIVE_SALES_HANDLE`, `features/contact/core/contact-copy.ts`) points it at that profile's availability and discovery-call flow (#80) with no third-party embed. **(c) Owner to supply:** the legal name, company number, registered address and support hours (`XXXX-XXXX`, marked "not yet published" for screen readers), and to confirm the reply targets, which are phrased as targets ("We aim to…") because no support-desk data exists to state a measured one. **(d) Guests cannot attach files** (D). **(e) No malware scanner:** "Checking the file" is the byte sniff and the type rule, as for every upload on the platform (wave 8 H3). **(f) No operator desk:** requests are read by operators through SQL or the service role; `ops.set_contact_request_status` exists with no UI, and `contact.received` has no action URL until a desk does. **(g) No acknowledgement email to the sender** — the confirmation panel is the receipt. **(h) Support topics** are a local list (`CONTACT_SUPPORT_TOPICS`); once P2's `editorial.help_categories` merges they should be read from it, one value per category slug. **(i) Not verified live:** the tables, bucket, enum value and catalog row reach the shared database only on a reset after merge; the live write, the live attachment promotion and operator notification were verified by a rolled-back probe (`supabase/probes/contact_requests.sql`, 81 PASS) and the UI on the gate-off path, including the committed state matrix `apps/web/tests/e2e/contact.spec.ts` (`deno task test:e2e`, launch config `web-contact-e2e`). PUBLIC_ROUTES P4 (`/about`); builds work-order ruling (f) and the owner's 2026-10-17 ruling "real server-side aggregates only, hidden below `public_metrics_min_n` (default 10)". FLAGS (a)–(i) for a human.** **(A) SOURCE.** `finance.public_metrics()` (`00001265`, its own file — no shared region fits a public-site read): `SECURITY DEFINER`, `STABLE`, `search_path = ''`, EXECUTE for `service_role` only (`00002510` `[about_metrics]`). It returns aggregates only and applies the threshold IN SQL, each figure by its OWN count, so a figure resting on fewer than n rows comes back `NULL` with its count — a sum over one escrow is that escrow's amount, which is row-level data. The per-currency parts of the protected total are gated by the total's count only: they reach the service role alone, and the public sees them only folded into one converted, coarsened total (C). Rejected: service-role table reads (rows over the wire to be summed in TypeScript; PostgREST aggregates are off) and an anon-granted view in the `search.platform_stats` mould (small unthresholded figures public, freshness not the service's). **(B) COUNTING.** Value protected = `amount_cents` (principal; no deadline bonus) of escrows `funded` · `held` · `disputed` · `released`, all time; `refunded` is excluded because refunded money can be escrowed again and would be counted twice. Stages delivered = `projects.project_stages` `approved` / `paid` (archived included — a delivered stage stays delivered) WITH MONEY EVIDENCE: in a non-personal project (#192 — no money) and with at least one escrow `released` to a payee. The stage's own word is not enough — "Users can manage stages of own projects" lets the owner write a stage's `status` and `completed_at` directly (confirmed in a rolled-back run: an escrow-less `open` stage set to `paid`), so one Client could otherwise self-declare stages delivered; the escrow is written by the settlement doors alone. Funding → approval = per delivered stage, hours from its first released escrow's `created_at` to its LAST release, `max(released_at)` (stamped by `fn_release_ticket_escrow`, definer-only), falling back to the owner-writable `completed_at` only where no released escrow carries a `released_at` (the seed's do not); the median by `percentile_cont(0.5)`, published to 0.1 h. The fee = the `platform_fee_bp` param, never a negotiated rate. Each figure is held to the threshold by its OWN count: protected escrows; delivered stages; delivered stages with an interval. **(C) CURRENCY.** Amounts are stored in their origin currency and the function never sums across currencies (`[{currency, amount_minor}]`). One currency → that exact total, unconverted. Several → each converted into the `base_currency` param (GBP) at the newest `finance.fx_rates` observation through `FxService` — the product's read-time display rule (finance-model.md §11) — and summed; if any currency has no rate the total is withheld (logged), never understated by dropping it nor overstated by relabelling it. A row whose currency is not a three-letter code withholds the total too (logged), rather than being dropped. PUBLISHED COARSENED: the service floors the total's whole major units to TWO significant figures before it leaves (`coarsenPublishedTotal`; `$151,000` → `$150,000`), keeping the agreed `amountMinor: int` shape — the threshold keeps one escrow out of a single read, and this keeps it out of the difference of two hourly reads (the step is 1–10% of the total, so a funded or refunded escrow shows only as whole steps, coarser as the platform grows); floored, never rounded up. Display then rounds DOWN to whole units (compact, three figures, above a million; the exact published amount is spoken). **(D) THRESHOLD.** `public_metrics_min_n` = 10 in `00005001` `[about_metrics]`; missing, a string, zero or below 1 → the literal 10 (`PUBLIC_METRICS_DEFAULT_MIN_N`) with `min_n_configured = false`, which the service logs on every live read; a fractional value floors. **(E) SERVICE + CONTRACT.** `PublicMetricsService.get(): Promise<ServiceResult<PublicMetrics>>` (`packages/backend/services/marketing/`), the shape kept EXACTLY as agreed with the landing track: `asOf` · `minN` · `platformFeeBp` (always) · `totalValueProtected {amountMinor, currency} | null` · `stagesDelivered | null` · `medianFundingToApprovalHours | null` (Zod `PublicMetricsSchema`, `@projective/types/marketing`). Cached one hour in its own `ArcCache` under the anonymous tenant (the answer is the same for every visitor); concurrent misses share one in-flight read (single flight); a failure is a 503 / 502, never cached for the hour but held 30 s (`PUBLIC_METRICS_FAILURE_HOLD_MS`) so a failing database is not re-scanned on every request. `GET /api/public/metrics` = the flat `{ ok, …PublicMetrics }` envelope via `defineReadRoute` (`public-metadata`, strong ETag). Behind `FINANCE_BACKEND_LIVE` (the data's domain); off, the same fold runs over `public-metrics-fixtures.ts` — the function's output on the seeded shared DB on 2026-10-17 21:07 UTC (8 escrows: 5 held, 3 released, all USD; 2 paid stages), read inside a rolled-back transaction with the threshold lifted to 1, re-held to the default 10 — so on the development seed only the fee prints, which is the honest answer. **(F) PAGE, where the work order and the binding docs differ — the docs win (as #273).** The diagram's colours follow the theme clock (`--dur-slow`) and only the token's move takes `--dur-medium` (§B.5 simultaneous crossfade); "Talk to sales (tonal)" is `severity="neutral" variant="outlined"` (Button has no tonal variant; #157 flag (l)); "Start a project" is the one filled `--primary` (tier 3) and goes to `/join` for a guest, `/projects?create=1` (the Quick-Init modal) when signed in; the metric tile is feature-local, not `StatTile` (it needs the timestamp slot and a `deno test` render); the page controller is `features/marketing/about/routes/AboutPage.tsx` (the work order's `about/AboutPage.tsx` sits outside the seven-folder rule). The work order's "RLS on every table" is NOT literally true: five tables run with RLS off — `security.feature_flags`, `security.audit_logs`, `security.turnstile_verifications`, `security.refresh_tokens`, `integrations.consent_states` — each holding no `anon` / `authenticated` privilege (checked on the shared DB 2026-10-17), so the page says "every table a visitor or a member can query". (d) **Two "stages delivered" on the public site.** The landing hero's `search.platform_stats.stages_delivered` counts `projects.stage_assignments` `completed`, unthresholded, and its `paid_out_minor` is USD-only although its comment says base currency; `/about` counts `project_stages` `approved` / `paid` above the threshold. Pick one definition (the landing track's L4 reads `PublicMetricsService`). The old allow-all `static/robots.txt` is deleted (the static-files middleware would have answered first). **(H) DOCS.** PRODUCT_SPEC sitemap (`/sitemap.xml`, `/robots.txt`; the `/legal` and `/articles` rows already moved to Public per rulings (a)/(b), no duplicates); ROUTING (rows for `/about`, `/feedback`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/robots.txt`; reserved handles: `/changelog` and `/feedback` now routed, `robots.txt` / `sitemap.xml` served); DESIGN_SYSTEM §C.1 (every P0–P7 component and page view now named once — `DocumentPage` / `DocumentPageView` / `JsonLd` / `PageMetaTags`, `PublicFooter` + `FooterLinkGroups`, `IntentFieldsets`, `AboutView`, the help pages, `ArticleMeta` and the article views; Button's anchor form; `LegalDate` retired) and Part D (the guest footer is a sibling of `<main>`); SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE (the sitemap reads the editorial surfaces through their own services); `database/ops/Functions.md`, `database/editorial/Tables.md`; #270–#278 all present in this file and indexed. **(I) VERIFIED.** `deno task check`, `deno task lint`, `deno task test:unit` (only the four known `theme-engine.test.ts` failures); the fixture road (`EDITORIAL` / `COMMUNITY` / `CONTACT` / `FINANCE` / `NEWSLETTER` / `LOGGING_BACKEND_LIVE=false`) at 375 / 768 / 1280, light and dark, reduced motion; the migration chain on a throwaway `public_routes_chain` database in the shared instance (prerequisites from a schema-only dump of the live one, filtered to the Supabase-managed schemas; all 122 migrations and 13 seeds; probes `contact_requests` 81 PASS, `help_centre` 37, `function_grants` 10, `reserved_handles` 18, 0 FAIL; a rolled-back check that all nine topics are accepted and the five retired ones refused with `22023` naming `topic`), then dropped. Nothing ran against the `postgres` database but a read-only schema dump. **(J) THE SMOKE AND THE BUDGET (P8 items 4–5).** `apps/web/tests/e2e/public-routes.spec.ts`, run by `deno task test:e2e:public` (its own task, so `test:e2e`'s catalogue and contact suites are untouched) against the `web-public-e2e` launch config (port 13380; the editorial, community, contact, finance and newsletter gates off — the fixture road, so nothing is read from or written to the new tables; every non-GET `/api/**` but `/api/auth/*` is aborted). Twenty-five pages — `/legal`, its six documents and `/legal/terms?compare=1.0`; `/help`, a category, two articles and `/help?q=escrow` (the search dialog); `/contact` for each of the four intents; `/about`; `/changelog` and `/changelog/0.17.0`; `/articles` and two articles; `/feedback`; `/about?feedback=open` (the drawer) — each at 375, 768 and 1280 px, light and dark (`colorScheme` + `localStorage.theme`), with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: 150 visits, each asserting a 200, no console error or uncaught throw, no subresource that fails or answers ≥ 400 (so an unresolved `/test_images` path fails), exactly one `<h1>`, a `<title>` and `lang`, one `main` / `banner` / `contentinfo` and at least one `navigation` landmark (counted by role, so the header/footer scoping is the browser's own), at least one JSON-LD block and every block parsing, no horizontal scroll, and axe-core 4.10.3's WCAG 2.0–2.2 A/AA rules — a test-only `npm:axe-core` import evaluated over CDP (never in the import map; its only footprint is a `deno.lock` entry, as `playwright-core`'s is); for the two overlays: opened by their address, `aria-modal`, Escape closes them, their parameter leaves the address, and axe runs again on the page beneath. Plus the PDF (`application/pdf`, `%PDF-`), the RSS feed and the sitemap (well-formed per the browser's `DOMParser`; all 72 sitemap URLs on-origin and answering 200) and robots.txt (the API, `/legal/workspace/`, `feedback=open`, a `Sitemap:` line). One full-page screenshot per visit. axe-core loaded, so the keyboard-only fallback was not needed; the overlays' Escape path is scripted. **Found and fixed:** (1) the guest header's brand link had no accessible name below 900 px (the wordmark is `display: none` there and the mark `aria-hidden`) — it carries `aria-label="Projective"`, its visible word (`SiteHeader.island.tsx`); (2) the help search dialog's body was a scroll region with nothing focusable in it (the options are `tabindex=-1` under `aria-activedescendant`) — the listbox itself now scrolls (`.hc-palette__list`, the body a flex column it shrinks into), so the region that scrolls is the combobox's own popup and the status line stays put; (3) `@projective/ui` `SpeedDial` (the dev context switcher's, on every page in development) put `<li>`s and `role="tooltip"` spans inside its `role="menu"` — the `<li>`s are `role="none"` and the hover labels `aria-hidden` (they repeat each action's `aria-label`). **Reported, not failed:** a `color-contrast` failure whose colours are exactly the page's own `--on-primary` on `--primary` while that pair itself is under 4.5:1 — today `#ebfdff` on `#00929e`, 3.57:1, dark only, on every filled primary button and the header's Join CTA (52 page × variant hits) — the brand-tone split that the four pre-existing `theme-engine.test.ts` failures already pin and that is held for the owner (flag (k)); the spec computes the pair from the page, so it stops reporting the moment the pair clears AA, and any other colour pair fails the run. **Budget:** `/articles/no-hold-no-work` and `/help/escrow-and-payments/fees` on a mid-tier phone (375 px, DPR 2, touch, 4× CPU throttle over CDP, Lighthouse's slow-4G: 150 ms RTT, 1.6 Mbps down): CLS **0** while loading — on the dev server and on a production build (`deno task build`, served on 13381 and selected with `E2E_PUBLIC_BUDGET_BASE_URL`) — and at most 0.0012 after reading to the end (the header bar condensing on scroll), against 0.05; no render-blocking third-party resource and no third-party request at load (the fonts are self-hosted; the one `placehold.co` figure is lazy and sized). The same 150-visit matrix also passes against the production build. **FLAGS — for the owner.** (a) **Going live.** The `editorial` and `community` schemas and every P1–P7 table, function, bucket and catalog row exist only in migrations: after merging, the shared stack needs `supabase stop && supabase start` (PostgREST must expose the two schemas, #274 (a)) and `deno task db:reset`; then, per environment, `EDITORIAL_BACKEND_LIVE=true` (help, changelog, articles from the database), `COMMUNITY_BACKEND_LIVE=true` (helpfulness votes, the feedback board), `NEWSLETTER_BACKEND_LIVE=true` (now writing `community.newsletter_subscriptions`; production refuses the footer's and the changelog's subscribe with a 503 while it is off — (K)), `CONTACT_BACKEND_LIVE=true` (production refuses `/contact` with a 503 while it is off), `CONTACT_CRON_SECRET` set to a real secret (the hourly `contact-attachment-sweep` door), and `APP_URL` as the public origin (canonicals, JSON-LD, the sitemap and robots). `PROJECTIVE_SALES_HANDLE` is not an env key: it is a constant in `features/contact/core/contact-copy.ts` (`null`, so Book a discovery call stays disabled with its reason) — set it once a Projective sales profile exists. Nothing on the live road was exercised in this build. (b) **Placeholders that need real content:** every legal document (drafts with `reviewedAt` null — the disclosure and `noindex` stay, and the sitemap lists none, until a lawyer signs off; the reconstructed 1.0 baselines; the data controller's identity, address and DPO, #270 (a), (b), (h)); the `/about` founders (#277 (a) — no band is drawn until they exist, (K)); the contact page's entity facts `XXXX-XXXX` (#276 (c)); Projective's social profile URLs (`SOCIAL_PROFILES` in `PublicFooter`); the articles' team byline (#271 (a)); the changelog's 24 release captures and the feed's social card, all `placehold.co` (#278 (a)) — the grey "Team console" and "Business spend" blocks on `/changelog/0.17.0`; and the articles' covers, stock photography from `/test_images` (`banner_*`), with their inline `placehold.co` figures (#271 (b)) — `/articles` leads with a car photograph as the cover of "Ending a stage early, fairly". (c) **CLOSED by #295** (a `PageCanvas` footer slot after `</main>`, verified signed in at 375 / 768 / 1280). **Signed-in public pages still have no `contentinfo`:** `UserShell` mounts the footer at the end of the canvas's `<main>` (`bodyFooter` → `PageCanvas`), the only mount point that survives its fixed surface fills; moving it out needs a `PageCanvas` footer slot and a signed-in visual check, which this build did not run (no authenticated session on the fixture road). (d) **The sitemap leaves out member content** — profiles (`/:handle`), listings (`/view/:id`) and member posts — each behind its own visibility rules; they want a sitemap index of their own. Start with these", #175) lists member posts above "All help articles → `/help`" — two sources under one heading. (i) #270 (p)'s third gap — the meta rail only from `--bp-xl` of frame — stands, per #273 (c). (j) **Done — see (J):** the Playwright smoke at 375 / 768 / 1280 with axe-core, and the CLS budget on `/articles/[slug]` and `/help/<article>`. (k) **The brand pair fails AA in dark:** `--on-primary` `#ebfdff` on `--primary` `#00929e` is 3.57:1 — every filled primary button and the header CTA on every public page in dark mode. (l) **What the smoke does not cover:** signed-in public pages (no session on the fixture road — see (c)); the accessibility overlays (`pj.a11y` high contrast, OpenDyslexic, CVD) — the matrix is the OS channels only; the live road (flag (a)); and `/` (the landing track's). (m) **Page edges across the public family:** `/contact`, `/articles` and `/feedback` run a `--container-xl` frame with a `--space-4` gutter, so at 1280 their content starts near 32px while the footer's starts at 64px (`--lp-pad-x`, `clamp(1.25rem, 5vw, 5rem)`). Matching them wants one shared public-page gutter token (with `max-inline-size` widened by both gutters so wide screens agree too); it was not changed in the review because it moves `/contact`'s 60rem split from about 992px to about 1067px of viewport and the signed-in canvas, where a viewport-based gutter behaves differently, cannot be checked on the fixture road (see (c)). (n) **The footer between 901 and ~1180px** still wraps several labels onto two lines (each stack is ~130px at 1024): the review's three-lane layout fixes 1280 and above and narrows the problem below it (stacks were ~105px at 1024 before), but a layout for that band — the nav full-width earlier, say — is a design call. **(K) REVIEW FIXES (2026-10-18).** (1) **`/about` founders:** three stock portraits of real people captioned "Co-founder · Role — XXXX" presented strangers as Projective's founders; `ABOUT_FOUNDERS` is now empty, `AboutView` draws no founders band while it is (an optional `founders` prop lets a render test draw it), the bands after the walkthrough re-pair their tones so two of one tone never meet (the test walks all seven or eight), and `about-content.test.ts` refuses any later founder with `XXXX` copy or a `/test_images` portrait (#277 (a) updated). | 280 | **The landing page's scoped design-system exemption — the `lp-` namespace on `features/landing/**`, the `/` route and the `/features` route, raw WebGL2 with zero new dependencies, and a leak test (2026-10-17). Decision (g) of `flows/PUBLIC_ROUTES_BUILD_PROMPTS.md` §0.1; product-owner ruling on L0 STEP 0 question 5.** **CONTEXT.** The landing track (L0–L6) builds a deliberately off-system marketing home page. Root `CLAUDE.md` §3 makes token-only CSS, no UI-library dependencies, the anti-card rules and the `backdrop-filter` limit merge gates everywhere, so without a ruling every L-prompt PR fails review. **RULING.** [1] scoped exemption · [2] wider (every marketing route) · [3] none → "Scoped exemption (Recommended)". **(A) SCOPE.** Exempt paths are exactly `apps/web/features/landing/**`, the `/` route (`routes/(public)/index.tsx`) and the `/features` route (`routes/(public)/features.tsx`) — nothing else, the rest of `features/marketing/` included. **(B) EXEMPT, inside the namespace only:** its own palette, type scale, radii, shadows, glass / `backdrop-filter`, gradients and glows as `--lp-*` custom properties in `features/landing/styles/lp-theme.css`, scoped to `.lp-root` (and `.lp-portal` on any panel the overlay layer moves to `<body>`, since a portal leaves `.lp-root`); cards, bento grids and decorative containers; motion beyond the app's spring set (scroll reveals, WebGL, pointer effects). Every class is `lp-` BEM and every token `--lp-*`; light and dark key to the app's `data-theme`, high contrast to both of its channels, and the dyslexic overlay remaps every `--lp-font-*` to `--font-*` (`flows/LANDING.md` §3.6). **(C) NEVER EXEMPT** (the §2.0 addendum): accessibility — WCAG 2.2 AA contrast on every text-over-effect, a full keyboard path, visible focus (FLAG (b)), ARIA on every interactive demo; both reduced-motion channels (`prefers-reduced-motion` AND `data-motion="reduced"`: no WebGL animation, no autoplay, no scroll-jacking, instant state changes); islands never touch Supabase (demos are pure simulations over typed fixtures and write nothing); thin route, fat service, `ServiceResult<T>`, Zod at every boundary; security (the CSP is unchanged — WebGL shader compilation is not eval, nothing external is fetched); every claim true per #281; SEO (SSR text, one h1, JSON-LD, meta, "escrow" per #283); the performance budget (LANDING.md §7, enforced in L6); the global asset rules (placehold.co, seeded URLs or `/test_images` copies, no stock). **(D) DEPENDENCY POLICY.** [1] raw WebGL2, zero dependencies · [2] one pinned WebGL helper → "Raw WebGL2 (Recommended)": the B1 constellation is hand-written WebGL2 (shaders as tagged template strings in `features/landing/core/shaders/*.ts`); `three` (pinned in `deno.json` for the file inspector) is NOT imported anywhere on `/` or `/features`, and no new npm or jsr dependency lands in this track. **(E) LEAK TEST.** L1 adds a `deno task test:unit` gate (on the pattern of `features/workspaces/styles/styles.gate.test.ts`: comment blanking, file:line failures) that fails on any `lp-` class or `--lp-*` token in `apps/web/**` or `packages/**` outside the exempt paths; L6 also diffs the built CSS of app routes against the pre-track build. **CONSEQUENCES.** Every app gate still applies to every other surface, and to app components rendered inside the landing (the board mock keeps the app's tokens so it matches the product — layout D's own risk). `design-system/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` Part E gains an "Off-system surfaces" note and `business/PRODUCT_SPEC.md` §Visual Identity points at `flows/LANDING.md`. **FLAGS for a human.** (a) **The namespace is already taken outside the exempt paths**: `features/marketing/components/PublicFooter.tsx` (`lp-footer*`, :99-193), `FooterLinkGroups.island.tsx`, `NewsletterForm.island.tsx`, `RecentlyViewed.island.tsx`, `marketing/styles/footer.css` (`.lp-footer` with local `--lp-*`), `marketing/styles/hero-search.css:258` (`--lp-hair-strong`), `shell/styles/guest-shell.css:224` and a comment at `packages/ui/styles/index.css:447`; the old `marketing/styles/landing.css` (`.lp{--lp-*}`) goes with the retired components in L1. As written the leak test fails on day one. Proposed: L1 renames the surviving footer block to `.site-footer` / `--sf-*` (pairing the existing `.site-header`; both free) — it needs the owner's OK because the footer is #13's and renders on every public page; the alternative is an allowlist in the test. (b) **Visible focus vs the no-focus-ring directive — a NEW doc-vs-doc conflict, OPEN.** The addendum's never-exempt list (and this ruling) requires visible focus; `apps/web/styles/global.css:210-282` strips every outline and focus box-shadow app-wide by product-owner directive (an accepted WCAG 2.4.11 regression; #217 (n); #153 is the precedent for a scoped exception). LANDING.md §3.6 carries both recipes — (A) a ring restored inside `lp-` only, (B) a directive-compliant border, tint and underline treatment — and L1 ships no focus styling until the owner picks one. (c) **Board-mock tokens.** L3 asks for a theme bridge mapping app tokens to `--lp-*` inside `.lp-demo`; layout D's risk ("the mock must match the real UI") argues for keeping the app's tokens, which LANDING.md proposes — that inherits #183 (e) (dark `--primary` / `--on-primary` at 3.57:1 on any real teal `Button` in the theatre or stage). Needs a ruling. (d) The OS high-contrast channel stops matching once hydration writes `data-contrast="normal"` (`packages/ui/system/core/context.ts:140`; `apps/web/utils/a11y-context.ts:104-105`) — pre-existing app behaviour the `lp-` selectors mirror; not fixed here. (e) `@media` units follow `packages/ui` (px) while #251 (a) is open. (f) No webfont exists and `font-src` is `'self' data:` (`apps/web/utils/csp.ts:79`): the type uses system stacks, a system serif included; any self-hosted OFL face (Newsreader or Fraunces; Geist or Inter) is a font-asset decision the owner has not taken. (g) **`.lp-portal` widens the owner's scope**: answer 5 scopes the tokens to `.lp-root`; the spec adds `.lp-portal` on any panel the overlay layer moves to `<body>` (a portal leaves `.lp-root`) — an extension the owner may veto (LANDING.md §9 row 24). | `flows/LANDING.md` §0, §3, §7, §9 · `flows/PUBLIC_ROUTES_BUILD_PROMPTS.md` §0.1 (g), §2.0, L1 · `design-system/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` Part E (Off-system surfaces) · `business/PRODUCT_SPEC.md` §Visual Identity · `apps/web/styles/global.css` · Decisions #13 / #153 / #157 / #183 / #217 / #251 |
| 281 | **Landing claims rule — every sentence on `/` and `/features` is shipped and true, a live metric, or labelled "Coming soon"; the claims table in `flows/LANDING.md` §5 is the gate L6 walks (2026-10-17). Decision (h) of `flows/PUBLIC_ROUTES_BUILD_PROMPTS.md` §0.1, recorded with L0.** **CONTEXT.** The landing draft stated things the code does not back — decision (h) lists "0% escrow capital lost", "assembly under 4 minutes", "Deno/Rust architecture", "virus-checked files", "cryptographic IP deeds", royalties, tool integrations, the tax-pot auto-skim and competitor fees — and a claim audit of payments, work and teams run for L0 on 2026-10-17 found more, several in the work order itself. **RULING.** (A) Every factual sentence is one of: **Shipped** (proved by file:line or a decision #); **Live metric** (rendered only from P4's `PublicMetricsService` at or above its `minN` threshold, hidden — never padded, zeroed or estimated — below it); **Coming soon** (labelled on the page); **Model** (describes a way of working, names no company, states no figure); **Page fact** (true by the landing's own construction, proved by a test). (B) The claims table (`LANDING.md` §5, 109 rows) is the gate: every copy-deck sentence carries a tag that resolves to a row; a sentence with no proof is deleted, and the deletions are listed (§5.1, 54 rows) so L6 fails the page if one renders. (C) **Competitor figures are excluded**: no sourced, dated public citation was supplied, so "Why it's different" compares working models, not companies. (D) Live numbers come from P4 only; `LandingPayload.stats` / `search.platform_stats` never render. (E) L6 walks the table sentence by sentence against the rendered page and pastes it into its report. **WHAT THE AUDIT CHANGED IN THE COPY.** "Held safely until you approve" → "the team is paid when you approve" (approval is not the only release path); The spec wins on a business rule (§0). **(B) BUILT.** `fn_open_workload_report` now suspends. The ticket becomes `reported_hidden` with its assignee and held escrow kept, and `hidden_until` is stamped on the ticket and, newly, on the report: the expiry sweep reads the report's value and nothing used to set it. `projects.fn_resume_reported_ticket(ticket, report)` (internal) ends one report's suspension: the ticket goes back to `in_progress` when it is still suspended on that report and still held, and the countdown is lifted either way. The client answers by raising $W_i$: `fn_ticket_immutability_guard` lets a non-assignee raise (never lower) a `reported_hidden` ticket's `workload_intensity`, and `trg_adjust_workload_report` (`AFTER UPDATE OF workload_intensity`) resolves the report `adjusted` and resumes the work. The same guard refuses the reporter any `status` or $W_i$ change while suspended (`42501`). `fn_resolve_expired_workload_reports` and `fn_flag_bad_faith_report` resume the work instead of leaving the ticket in the backlog. Because a suspended ticket now carries a hold, `cancel_stage_fair_exit` (and the preview's `tickets_to_cancel`) cancels it with its stage and lifts the countdown, and `remove_project_member` settles it like any held ticket (§Freelancer Removal Mid-Ticket). Probe `supabase/probes/workload_report_suspension.sql`: it fails on the old functions and passes on these. `function_grants`, `fair_exit_settlement`, `escrow_settlement_authority`, `business_authority`, `ledger_immutability`, `team_search_workload` and `workspace_detail_payload` pass with the new definitions applied. Docs: `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` (the section above), `PRODUCT_MANAGEMENT.md` §3.6 rule 7, `database/projects/{Functions,Tables,Policies}.md`. No schema or Zod change. **FLAGS for a human:** (a) **The expiry sweep is not scheduled.** No `ops.scheduled_jobs` row runs `fn_resolve_expired_workload_reports` (or `fn_release_expired_claims`), so until one does, a suspended ticket waits for the client's raise, an audit or a settlement. Recommend registering both (Decision #203). (b) **"Both parties incur a penalty"** on non-response, but the sweep penalises only the client. (c) **Ruled here; please confirm.** After the window lapses, or once a report is dismissed, the work resumes at the original $W_i$ (the spec says only that the ticket is hidden for 48 h). A report may be filed only while the ticket is claimed or in progress. (d) **A settlement leaves the report open.** If the client approves, Fair-Exits or removes the freelancer during the window, the report stays `open`, and the sweep later penalises the client for not adjusting a ticket they settled. (e) **Only the owner can answer.** The _View tickets_ arm hides a suspended ticket from every project-access viewer, and _Manage tickets_ admits only the owner and the assignee, so a business's other reviewers can neither see the ticket nor raise its $W_i$. (f) **Seen in passing, not fixed.** `fn_ticket_immutability_guard` exempts the assignee entirely, so a freelancer can rewrite their own claimed ticket's `unit_price_cents` (verified by rolled-back execution). `finance.fn_hold_ticket_escrow` prices the ticket's next-stage hold (the Chain Reaction, #210) from that column, so the client's wallet can be held at a price they never agreed; releasing it still needs approval. **CLOSED by #291.** |

The spec wins on a business rule (§0). **(B) RULED — the assignee keeps no content edits.** Once claimed, title, description, `text_description`, `unit_price_cents`, `required_stages` and `workload_intensity` bind both parties. The description is the scope the client pays for and approves against, and a $W_i$ change goes through a workload report (#290), not an edit. The assignee keeps everything that is not a term: the checklist (`tasks`), moves between the work columns of its own stage, submissions. (1) The terms lock binds both parties: the client keeps its `P0001` message, the assignee gets `42501`. (2) A claimed ticket's `current_stage_id` moves only with review authority, on every path (`42501`). (3) An `INSERT` that names an assignee needs review authority (`42501`). (4) A statement run as `anon` / `authenticated` may not change `payment_status` or `total_amount_paid`, and an `INSERT` starts them `unpaid` / `0`. Every other rollback-safe probe — 56, with the three dblink/concurrency probes left out — gives the same result with #290's tree spliced in as with this one. `function_grants` fails identically on both, on #290's two new functions, whose `00002510` REVOKEs the shared DB has not had. The shared local DB was **not** reset. No schema or Zod change. **FLAGS for a human:** (a) **Stacked on #290's branch** (`claude/workload-report-no-release`), which rewrote the same function; merge that first. (b) **`move_ticket` still lets anyone with project access move any ticket between status columns**, including another freelancer moving someone else's claimed ticket. It moves no money (completion needs review authority), but no rule says who may move whose card. (c) **`due_date` is not locked after a claim**, for either party. Another freelancer could move anyone's work, the client's #94 lock was board-only, and a move back to Claimed let the client get delivered work refunded (2026-10-17). CLOSES #291 (b).** **(A) THE DEFECT, reproduced by execution** (rolled back on the seed with #290's and #291's definitions spliced in; ticket `1d760dab…` `in_progress`, 800,000 held for a freelancer without review authority). `projects.move_ticket` is `SECURITY DEFINER`, so RLS never sees its write, and its only guards were `has_project_access` and, for Done, `can_review_project`. (1) **Another freelancer**, added to the project in the transaction, moved the ticket to `todo`, `backlog`, `in_review`, `claimed`, `cancelled` and `reported_hidden`. After `reported_hidden`, #290's suspension guard locked the **real assignee** out of their own ticket. Their direct `PATCH` was filtered by _Manage tickets_. (2) **The client** moved the ticket under way to any column, to another stage and to Done, through `move_ticket` and by a direct `PATCH`. `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` §Ticket Movement's lock (#94) was enforced only by the board's `ticketWorkLocked`. (3) **Money.** A move into `claimed` restamps `claimed_at` (`fn_ticket_claim_before`), and `projects.fn_release_expired_claims` refunds an expired claim to the client in full. The freelancer handed the work back for review, and the client moved it to `claimed`. The sweep then refunded the whole **800,000** to the client and put the ticket back in New, so the freelancer was paid nothing for delivered work. (4) **The assignee** moved their own ticket to `backlog`, `cancelled` or `reported_hidden`, on either path. **(B) THE RULE**, taken from §Ticket Movement (#94) and §The Claim-and-Commit Protocol (a claimed ticket is soft-locked to its freelancer, who moves it into Doing). It refines both and contradicts neither. Only the assignee or review authority moves a claimed ticket. The assignee moves it between `todo`, `in_progress` and `in_review`, and out of `claimed` into them. These are #291 (B)'s "moves between the work columns of its own stage", with `todo` kept because #291's probe moves the ticket there. New, Done, another stage and every other move are the client's. Review authority does not move it, by status or by stage, while it is `claimed` / `in_progress` (#94); from `in_review` (the hand-back) and `completed` it does. Nobody moves it **into** `claimed`, `cancelled` or `reported_hidden`. The claim enters `claimed`, the stage's cancellation (`cancel_stage_fair_exit`) enters `cancelled` and a workload report enters `reported_hidden`, and each settles or keeps the escrow on its own terms. Not gated: an unclaimed ticket, an unchanged status and stage (the client's plain save of a working ticket still passes), one person on both sides, `security.is_admin()`, a `NULL` `auth.uid()`. **(C) BUILT** (migrations edited in place). The rule is one predicate, `projects.fn_assert_ticket_move(project, assignee, from_status, to_status, from_stage, to_stage)` in `00001110`. It is `SECURITY INVOKER` and `STABLE`, raises `42501`, writes nothing, and `00002510` grants its `EXECUTE` to `authenticated`, because the INVOKER trigger calls it as that role. It has two callers. `move_ticket` (`00001120`) now reads its row `FOR UPDATE` and asks it before writing. `fn_ticket_immutability_guard` asks it for a statement run as `anon` / `authenticated` whose assignee is unchanged; a change of assignee is the reassign or release doors' to judge. Definer doors (`review_submission`, the Chain Reaction, Fair Exit, member removal, the TTL sweep, the workload report) are unaffected, because their `current_user` is their owner. #291's stage rule is untouched. `refusalFrom` (`live-writes.ts`) maps the predicate's sentences to a 403 in the database's words, not a 502 (unit test in `live-writes.test.ts`). No schema, Zod or Dev Context Switcher change: no new simulatable axis, and the persona and `fundingState` axes already drive the board lock. Docs: `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` §Ticket Movement, `PRODUCT_MANAGEMENT.md` §3.5 funding-scope row and §3.6 rule 8, `database/projects/Functions.md`. **(D) VERIFIED by execution, rolled back.** Probe `supabase/probes/ticket_move_authority.sql` fails on #291's definitions ("the client's move to Claimed was accepted, and the claim sweep then left the freelancer's delivered work refunded (800000 cents)"), and each of its later sections fails on them on its own too. It passes on these (55 checks). Regression sweep: 58 rollback-safe probes, base (#291's tree) against this one. 55 give identical output. `function_grants` fails identically on both, on #290's REVOKEs the shared DB lacks (as #291 reported). `service_instantiation` differs only in its random `prj-` slugs. `ticket_terms_payee_lock` passes 26 of 26 on both; one refusal is reworded because another freelancer's stage move now meets `move_ticket`'s own check first. The three dblink/concurrency probes were not run. The shared local DB was **not** reset. `deno task check` passes. **FLAGS for a human:** (a) **Stacked on #291's branch** (`claude/ticket-terms-payee-lock`, merged in), so merge #290 and #291 first. #292 is the deadline-bonus session's (`claude/lucid-shtern-9e815f`); its row and index line follow #291 too, so the two meet in a trivial conflict. (d) **The board's client seat is wider than review authority.** `viewerIsClientOf` seats a project `admin` participant (a delegate, #145) as the client, but `can_review_project` is the owner and the paying business's members. (f) **"Un-claim"** (`PRODUCT_MANAGEMENT.md` §3.2, Claimed → Ready) has no door. A move never was one, since it kept the assignee and the hold, and the assignee's move to New is now refused. |

An answer is optimistic: focus moves to the next row's Accept (else the previous, else the strip heading, which stays mounted once emptied), and a refused row comes back with an assertive `InlineNotice` routed by `details.reason` — `payout_not_ready` (with a tier-4 link to Settings → Verification), `persona` ("Teams are for freelancer accounts."), `seat_cap` ("This team is full.", newly typed by `inviteAnswerRefusal`). (b) Focus moves at press time, because the row leaves optimistically; a refused answer brings the row back with an announced notice but does not pull focus back to it. (c) "The first pending row" is applied literally: a first row whose Accept was refused keeps the tier-3 fill, so a retry stays possible — the alternative (fill the first row without a standing refusal) was not built. (d) `seat_cap` is typed on the invitee's door only: the inviter's seat-cap refusal (`invite_workspace_member`, C2's surface) still reaches the client as a bare 409 through `refusalFrom`, and a business accept refused by the `business_managers` plan gate (PK402) shows the server's own sentence. Needs a ruling and a row: Co-op is stake-weighted (fix finance-model §5) or forces an even split (the editor locks stakes to `evenStakes`). | 297 | **Screen sharing mode: one per-device switch that hides money, personal details, client identities and secrets while the screen is shown to an audience, painted from the first byte on every route (2026-10-19). Specified, not built. The Strategic Partner & Systems Consultant persona is added to root `CLAUDE.md` and cross-referenced in `documentation/CLAUDE.md` in the same change.** At the product owner's direction (one brief: the agent persona plus the Screen Sharing / Streamer Mode specification). **(A) WHERE IT IS SPECIFIED.** `PRODUCT_SPEC.md` §Screen Sharing & Privacy Mode (problem, creator and client-call workflows, the four treatments, boundaries, the commercial case) plus one bullet in §Settings. `SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md` §3 (a new directive) and §State Hydration → Screen sharing mode (state carriers, `_app.tsx` duties, standalone inheritance, three enforcement layers, keyboard, boundaries). `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` §B.14 (tokens, the four treatments, blur limits, reduced motion, the dense-surface ban) and Part E item 10. **(B) STATE.** `localStorage` `LocalKeys.SCREEN_SHARE` = `pj.local.screenShare` is the durable per-device copy, and its `storage` event flips every tab. Cookie `pj.screen_share=1` is a non-authoritative mirror: not HttpOnly, and able only to remove output. `routes/_middleware.ts` reads it into `ctx.state.screenShare`. `_app.tsx` writes the attribute, provides a per-request `ScreenShareContext` and runs a pre-paint restorer, the `pj.a11y` pattern. No route opts out of `_app.tsx`, so `(standalone)/inspect/[fileId]` inherits structurally. There is no column, migration or Zod row type; `SettingsSectionKey` gains `privacy`. It is not a Dev Context Switcher axis because the real control ships everywhere. **(C) DEPARTURES FROM THE BRIEF, decided here.** (1) The brief's literal `blur(12px)` and `scale(1.04)` become tokens `--obscure-blur` / `--obscure-bleed` (the token-only gate). (2) `filter: blur()` gets `backdrop-filter`'s containing-block rule, because the brief cited §3 for a property §3 did not govern: it goes on a media element in a clipping frame. (3) The brief named `GanttChart`; the component is `Gantt` (`@projective/ui/gantt`), and it paints on a `<canvas>`, which CSS cannot mask, so it and the Canvas2D charts read the store and paint masked figures themselves. (4) Dense surfaces swap in `ProgressiveImage`'s BlurHash instead of running a filter per item. (5) `MoneyView` currently writes `data-money-minor` and a figure-bearing `title` / `aria-label`, so masking must omit them; `CurrencyBridge` skips `data-money-masked`. **FLAGS for a human:** (a) Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + S is Firefox's Take Screenshot and Microsoft Edge's Web capture. Whether a page's `preventDefault` wins is browser-dependent. The menu row and Settings are the guaranteed paths; pick a fallback chord if the build's browser matrix fails. (b) A twelfth Settings section for one switch, as briefed, vs an entry under Appearance beside the other per-device overlays. Also open: whether Profile's "who can find you" and Messaging's read receipts cross-list there. (c) The press-and-hold **Show** on money fields and payment confirmations is an addition to the brief, so a person can verify an amount before committing it. It needs a product ruling. (d) The brief's solid block (`color: transparent`) reveals the text under `forced-colors: active`. The spec renders a placeholder instead of the text and adds `forced-color-adjust: none` to the CSS fallback. (e) A figure masked from the first byte stays masked after turning the mode off until the next navigation, because a forced reload would discard drafts. (f) Notification, toast and inbox copy that embeds pre-formatted amounts cannot be masked until the amount travels as structured data; audit needed. OS-level notifications are out of scope. (g) Island props still serialize money values into the document. This is accepted as outside the threat model (the frame is protected, devtools are not); secrets are omit-tier for that reason. (h) The `NumberInput` masking mechanism is left to the build; `type="password"` is ruled out because it invites password managers. (i) The competitive claim (no platform-wide equivalent on Fiverr or Upwork) is unverified and must be checked before any marketing use. **(D) BUILD OBLIGATIONS (same change as the code).** `SettingsSectionKey` `privacy` + registry entry `privacy.screen-share` + the `ROUTING.md` `/settings/:section` row · `LocalKeys.SCREEN_SHARE` · `utils/screen-share-context.ts` + test · `State.screenShare` · root `_middleware.ts` · `_app.tsx` · the `ScreenShareBridge` island · `shortcuts.ts` `isScreenShareShortcut` · the `UserActions.island.tsx` menu row + the top-bar eye-off mark · the `@projective/ui/utils` store + `Obscure` · `MoneyView` / `NumberInput` / `Gantt` / charts · `CurrencyBridge` skip · tokens in `packages/ui/styles/index.css` · `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` §C.1 roster. Files: root `CLAUDE.md` · `documentation/CLAUDE.md` · `business/PRODUCT_SPEC.md` · `architecture/SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md` · `design-system/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` |

The create modal still lands on `?section=media`, because it has just captured the title, model and category, so the cover is the next thing missing. **(B) HEADER:** the slug (`.cat-ws-head__id`, already in the URL) and the save state are removed from the header meta; the status `Tag` stays. **(C) RIG:** the save status moves to the start of `ListingActionRig`: a pip and meta text ("Saved · 2s ago", "Saving…", "Unsaved changes" + Save now, "Couldn't save" + Retry, "Changed in another tab" + Resolve, "Offline · not saved"). The `role="status"` announcer moves with it. Every secondary becomes a tier-4 neutral `outlined` circle with an `aria-label`, a portal `Tooltip` and `.ui-hit`: Duplicate (new here; it saves first, then opens the copy), Delete (was `text` danger, still #221-gated; its confirmation carries the danger), Archive (`archive-box`) and Pause. Publish is the only fill, icon and text. While the gate is closed it shows `lock`, stays `aria-disabled` (never native `disabled`, so hover and focus still open its Tooltip, which lists what is missing), and a press reveals the section that fixes the first missing line (`firstMissingSection`) and says the whole gate in the status. The visible gate sentence is gone; `#cat-ws-gate` stays as the visually hidden `aria-describedby` target (with `data-ready`). **(D) CELEBRATION:** `@projective/ui/feedback` gains `ActionCelebration` + `useActionCelebration`, extracted from the profile Follow burst; Follow now uses it, and the `.pf-burst` CSS is deleted. That flips 51 hints in 27 forms at once. Kept visible (`hintMode="inline"` / `note`): the contact message, profile headline and About counters; the idea composer's counter and personal-data warnings; the reserved-grant CONFIRM instruction; the Business Pro lock reasons (spend limit, per purchase, threshold, invoicing terms); and the wallet's empty-state reasons ("no other wallet", "no stage waiting", "save a card first"). The catalogue Edit form has its own field markup, so it gains `FieldHead` / `ToggleHint`, plus section intros and `OfferGroup` hints behind a "?" beside the heading. The live figure (Pipeline "Buyers see £x – £y a ticket"), statuses, empty states, cap messages, the conferencing "connect one" reason, the intake lock notice and the fixed-currency value stay visible. FLAGS: (a) a "?" button needs an island; every `FormControl` host with a hint was checked to be island-rendered, so a future server-only form with a hint would ship a dead "?" | 306 | **The team and business console: zoned lane, hubs, entity channels, the Files drive and the command-centre Overview (2026-10-20, owner rulings).** The owner chose, over the four conflicts put to them: the brief's full zoning (SUPERSEDES #228 (C) and #232's primary views), entity channels built now, real reads only on the Overview, and the brief's lane chrome (SUPERSEDES #222's band-only kebab placement and #228 (D)'s lane Invite). **(A) HUBS.** `NAV_HUBS` / `hubsForViewer` (module registry) gather the modules into lane rows: Core operations — Overview · Projects & work · Calendar & schedule · Files & docs · Catalogue (team) / Talent (business); Governance — Roster & members (`members` · `invitations` · `roles`) · Vault & finances (`finance` · `payouts`; a business's Wallet & spending: `finance` · `spend` · `billing`) · Analytics & standing; Settings (`settings` · `profile` · `verification`) in the lane footer. A hub is navigation only: every module keeps its route and gate, so no URL changed and no redirect was added. A multi-module hub is one header-band strip of LINK tabs (`hub-tabs.ts`: Roster & members = People · Invitations · Org chart · Roles; `/invitations` marks the Invitations tab); a single-module hub keeps its in-place sub-view tabs. The `messages` placeholder module is retired (its segment now 303s to the root). **(B) LANE.** Search moves to the head on both lanes (debounced typeahead over views, channels, projects and people; a person hit opens their drawer via `?member=<handle>`). The console head carries the crest (`VerificationStampBadge`, `stampForVerifiedOwner`), the verification words only while unverified, and the ONE entity kebab (`EntityMenu`: View public profile · Open in new tab · Copy profile link · Transfer ownership… / Leave… · Archive workspace…, danger). The band draws the same `EntityMenu` only while the lane is collapsed or hidden below `--bp-md` (`.wsp-headerband__menu` on the frame's lane mirror), so exactly one is reachable; the tier-4 Share profile is retired. The console footer is the acting switch as an outlined pill (its icon form in a compact lane), then circular tier-5 Invite member and Settings (`aria-label` + portal Tooltip + `.ui-hit`); the page rig carries Invite and Settings only in its phone layout (`rigLayouts` now answers a console's `withoutLane`). The roster index keeps its tier-2 `LaneCreateButton`. **(C) CHANNELS.** `comms.dm_threads` rows of kind `entity_channel`, owned by `(owner_type, owner_entity_id)`, named by `slug`, archived with `archived_at`; participants are the entity's active members, kept in step by triggers; every entity gets `general` (default, never archivable). Any active member may create one (cap 30 live); the creator or a `manage_settings` holder may archive. The list is `get_workspace_detail.channels`. Channels reuse the `/messages` chat stack (`ConversationChat` + `ChatComposer`) at `/teams/:h/channels/:channel` (and the business twin; `/channels` 303s to the default) and are excluded from the inbox, contacts, DM lookup, the under-18 shield, auto-replies, request promotion and add-members. Probe `supabase/probes/entity_channels.sql` (34 checks). **(D) FILES.** The `files` module is the entity's drive (`FileScope` `workspace`, subject = the entity id, seat checked by `org.get_acting_context_details` under the viewer's JWT; folders in `?path=`); any active member may read and upload, as RLS already allowed, without Acting as the entity. **(E) OVERVIEW.** A telemetry deck (`Grid` 13.75rem): a team's vault (payout holders), Σ Wᵢ of Σ members' own caps on a `ProgressRing`, the Standing rung, the weekly proposal allowance and members; a business's per-currency wallet tiles (Finance viewers), projects and members with manager seats. Then Needs attention (spend requests to decide, invitations out, engagements on hold, next milestones as the read words them), a 30-day cash flow from `/api/wallet/activity?w=<kind>:<id>` on the wallet's own `FlowAreaChart` (space reserved, CLS 0), the projects preview and the activity feed. One fill on the page still holds. FLAGS for a human: (a) **safety** — channels bypass the under-18 DM shield, so a minor in a team can be messaged by every member; (b) PII masking still applies in channels between members on a shared protected project; (c) no private channels, no channel notifications or mentions, no live mark-read (unread counts only move through the seed), archived history unreachable in the UI; (d) leaving a channel reuses `deleted_at`; (e) any member may create channels — gate on `manage_settings` if it becomes noise; (f) a channel's slug is its address, an exception to Decision #88's opaque prefixed slugs; (g) entity files no longer require Act as (a write-rule change in the files hub's invariant); the files API takes the entity id, not the handle (`org.business_profiles` has no client SELECT); (h) an upload into an ARCHIVED entity's drive is hidden in the UI but not refused by the server (`files.fn_owns_library` should refuse); (i) the Overview omits what no read answers — on-time delivery rate, quality streaks, items awaiting client review, discovery calls, a < 48h milestone warning (`due` is pre-formatted text) and per-member split distribution; (j) `detail.finance` is answered to every member, not only `manage_finances` holders — inconsistent with #233, for the backend owner; (k) the deck pins figures to their own currency while the cash flow arrives converted to the viewer's display currency; (l) the brief's Settings target `/settings?section=workspaces` does not exist — the gear opens the console's own Settings hub; (m) the brief's `WorkloadGauge`, `chart-geometry.ts` and `flows/ROUTING.md` do not exist (ProgressRing, `charts/geometry.ts` and `architecture/ROUTING.md` were used);
